definition_zh: 比较分析；对比研究；跨案例的比较方法；（法律、政策、文学等领域的）比较分析
definition_en: a method of study that sets two or more cases side by side and explains their similarities and differences
core_image: 两张摊开的表格并排放在桌上，同一栏的数据被红笔一对一对连起来
scene: 研究团队把六个城市的垃圾分类政策列成同一张表，逐项对照回收率与罚款额度。 Their comparative analysis of six cities showed that deposit schemes worked better than fines.
sceneCN: 这里指把多个案例并置、逐项对照的研究方法（第 1 个义项：跨案例的比较分析）；句意为他们对六座城市的比较分析显示押金制比罚款更有效。场景图取象：两张表格并排，同一栏的数据被红线两两相连。

pos.zh: 比较分析；对比研究（方法）
（法律）比较法上的分析
（政策、文学、历史等领域的）跨案例比较分析

derivatives.zh: 比较（由「一起」＋「使齐备」的拉丁构件合成，指把两物摆到一处量）
比较；对照（比较动词的名词形式，指动作或结论）
比较的；比较研究的（加表示「倾向于、用于」的形容词后缀）
分析（由希腊语「向上、彻底」的前缀加「松开」的动词构成，字面即把整体拆开看）
分析；解析（上述动词的名词形式，指拆解后看清结构）
分析者；分析师（加表示「人」的名词后缀）

senses.title: A cross-case method
senses.definition: a research method that examines several cases together in order to explain why they differ
senses.definitionCN: 把若干案例放在一起考察、以解释其差异的研究方法
senses.example: A comparative analysis of six cities showed that deposit schemes worked better than fines.
senses.exampleCN: 对六座城市的比较分析显示押金制比罚款更有效。
senses.why: One case can only describe; a second case gives the first something to be measured against.
senses.whyCN: 单一案例只能描述，第二个案例才给第一个提供可比的参照。

senses.title: Policy comparison
senses.definition: the systematic contrast of policies or institutions across jurisdictions
senses.definitionCN: 跨辖区对政策或制度所作的系统对照
senses.example: Their comparative analysis of welfare systems covered nine countries.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对福利制度的比较分析覆盖九个国家。
senses.why: Governments borrow from each other, and a structured comparison is how they decide what can travel.
senses.whyCN: 政府彼此借鉴，而结构化的比较正是判断哪些做法可以移植的办法。

senses.title: Comparative legal analysis
senses.definition: the study of how different legal systems treat the same question
senses.definitionCN: 研究不同法律体系如何处理同一问题的学问
senses.example: The article offers a comparative analysis of liability rules in three codes.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章对三部法典中的责任规则作了比较分析。
senses.why: Lawyers compare codes to see whether a rule is universal or merely local.
senses.whyCN: 法律人比较法典，是要看一条规则是普遍的，还是只是本地的。

senses.title: Comparative literature
senses.definition: the study of works from different languages or traditions in relation to each other
senses.definitionCN: 把不同语言或传统的作品放在一起考察的研究
senses.example: Her comparative analysis of two epics changed the reading of both.
senses.exampleCN: 她对两部史诗的比较分析改变了对两者的解读。
senses.why: A work seen beside a foreign cousin reveals conventions that a single tradition hides.
senses.whyCN: 作品旁边站着一个异国亲戚，才会露出单一传统所遮蔽的成规。

senses.title: Statistical group comparison
senses.definition: the formal contrast of two or more groups or conditions using quantitative data
senses.definitionCN: 用定量数据对两个或多个组别或条件所作的正式对照
senses.example: A comparative analysis of the two cohorts found no difference in survival.
senses.exampleCN: 对两个队列的比较分析未发现存活率差异。
senses.why: Numbers make comparison precise, and precision is what turns an impression into a finding.
senses.whyCN: 数字让比较变得精确，而精确正是把印象变成发现的关口。

senses.title: Comparative historical analysis
senses.definition: the comparison of historical cases or periods to identify causes and patterns
senses.definitionCN: 比较历史案例或时期，以找出原因与模式
senses.example: Comparative historical analysis explained why two revolutions ended so differently.
senses.exampleCN: 比较历史分析解释了两场革命为何结局迥异。
senses.why: History never repeats a case exactly, so the method compares near-cases to isolate what mattered.
senses.whyCN: 历史不会原样重演，方法便比较相近的案例，以分离出真正起作用的因素。

senses.title: A business cost comparison
senses.definition: a structured comparison of costs, benefits or options before a decision
senses.definitionCN: 决策前对成本、收益或备选方案所作的结构化比较
senses.example: The board asked for a comparative analysis of building versus leasing.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会要求对自建与租赁作一份比较分析。
senses.why: Firms compare options on one sheet so that a choice can be defended later.
senses.whyCN: 企业把备选方案放在一张表上比较，好让日后的选择有据可依。

senses.title: A research design
senses.definition: a formal design in which case selection and comparison are planned in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先规划好案例选择与对照方式的一种正式研究设计
senses.example: The course teaches comparative analysis as a design, not just a technique.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课把比较分析当作一种研究设计来教，而不只是一种技巧。
senses.why: Choosing which cases to compare decides the answer before the data arrive, so it belongs to design.
senses.whyCN: 选哪些案例来比，在数据到手前就决定了答案，所以它属于设计。

intro.en: Comparative analysis joins a Latin pair of words meaning 'to pair together' and a Greek one meaning 'to loosen up'. Both halves are well documented; the compound itself is a modern research label.
intro.cn: comparative analysis 把一个意为「配成对」的拉丁词与一个意为「拆开松开」的希腊词合在一起。两半的来源都有充分记录，这个复合词本身则是现代研究标签。

items.en: Latin comparare meant to bring two things level and measure one against the other, from com- 'together' and parare 'to make ready'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 comparare 意为把两物摆平、互相比量，由 com-「一起」与 parare「使齐备」构成。

items.en: The Latin adjective comparativus marked whatever serves for comparison, and English took it as comparative.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词 comparativus 标出用于比较之物，英语取为 comparative。

items.en: Greek analyein meant to loosen or break up a whole into its parts, from ana- 'up, throughout' and lyein 'to loosen'.
items.cn: 希腊语 analyein 意为把整体松开、拆成部分，由 ana-「向上、彻底」与 lyein「松开」构成。

items.en: The two words were joined in nineteenth-century research writing, when comparison became an organised method.
items.cn: 这两个词在十九世纪的研究写作中结合，当时比较已成为有组织的方法。

items.en: Anatomy, law and religion all developed a comparative method, and each needed a name for its core operation.
items.cn: 解剖学、法学与宗教学都发展出比较方法，各自都需要一个名称来指其核心操作。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase settled as a term for cross-case research in social science and policy.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这一短语定型为社会科学与政策研究中跨案例研究的术语。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two roots or looks close; the second group holds methods that are often put beside comparative analysis.
note.cn: 第一组或共享两个词根之一，或字形相近；第二组是常与比较分析并列的其他方法。

entries.definition: The adjective alone, naming work based on comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 单用的形容词，指以比较为基础的工作。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or the contrast, without the method's formality.
entries.definitionCN: 指比较动作或对照的名词，不含方法上的正式性。

entries.definition: The breaking up of a whole into parts, the second half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体拆成部分，是这个词组的后一半。

entries.definition: The adjective from analysis, describing a method that separates parts.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 analysis 的形容词，描述拆解部分的方法。

entries.definition: A deep study of one case, which comparative analysis deliberately contrasts with others.
entries.definitionCN: 对单一案例的深入研究所，比较分析有意拿它与别的案例对照。

entries.definition: A study of many cases at one moment, usually statistical rather than historical.
entries.definitionCN: 在同一时点考察许多案例，通常偏统计而非历史。

entries.definition: Comparing one's own performance with an external standard, common in management.
entries.definitionCN: 把自身表现与外部标准相比，常见于管理领域。

entries.definition: Combining the results of many studies into one statistical summary.
entries.definitionCN: 把许多研究的结果合成一个统计汇总。

entries.definition: Systematically coding texts, which may then be compared across sources.
entries.definitionCN: 对文本系统编码，随后可跨来源比较。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real two roots, the real fixed phrases and the real research family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的两个词根、真实固定说法与真实研究词族。

normal.en: The first half says pair together, the second half says break apart, so the phrase means pair cases and take them apart.
normal.cn: 前一半说配成对，后一半说拆开来，整个词组就是先把案例配对再拆开看。

normal.en: The family runs compare, comparison, comparative, analyse and analysis.
normal.cn: 同族词有 compare、comparison、comparative、analyse 与 analysis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: conduct a comparative analysis, cross-national comparative analysis, comparative legal analysis.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：进行比较分析、跨国比较分析、比较法律分析。

normal.en: The plural is comparative analyses, because the head noun is analysis.
normal.cn: 复数形式是 comparative analyses，因为中心词是 analysis。

normal.en: A comparative analysis always names its cases, since the second case is half the method.
normal.cn: 比较分析总要说明拿哪些案例来比，因为第二个案例就是方法的一半。

abstract.en: Comparison without analysis lists differences; analysis without comparison explains only one world.
abstract.cn: 只比较不分析，只是列出差别；只分析不比较，只解释一个世界。

abstract.en: The method's honesty lies in saying which cases were left out.
abstract.cn: 这一方法的诚实，在于说出哪些案例被漏掉了。

abstract.en: Analysis without a second case is a portrait; comparison without analysis is a list.
abstract.cn: 没有第二个案例的分析只是一幅肖像；没有分析比较只是一张清单。

examples.en: Their comparative analysis of the two health systems took four years.
examples.cn: 他们对两套医疗体系的比较分析花了四年。

examples.en: A comparative analysis of rainfall records explained the crop failure.
examples.cn: 对降雨记录的比较分析解释了这次歉收。

examples.en: The paper's comparative analysis is careful about what the cases share.
examples.cn: 这篇论文的比较分析对案例之间的共同点很谨慎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「先配对、再拆开」——把几个案例并排摆好，逐项对看：比较分析

root: comparative（拉丁语 comparativus ← comparare「配成对」← com-「一起」＋ parare「使齐备」）＋ analysis（希腊语 analyein「松开、拆解」← ana-「彻底」＋ lyein「松开」）。复合术语于十九世纪研究写作中成形，二十世纪定型为跨案例研究之名。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one method: a cross-case design, policy comparison, legal comparison, literary comparison, statistical groups, historical cases, business options, and the design itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种方法展开：跨案例设计、政策比较、法律比较、文学比较、统计分组、历史案例、商业备选方案，以及研究设计本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two open tables side by side, with entries in the same column joined by red lines.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张摊开的表格并排，同一栏的条目被红线两两连起。

branches.en: THE METHOD AND THE DESIGN: cases chosen and compared on purpose, not merely noticed.
branches.cn: 方法与设计：案例是被有意挑选、有意对照的，不只是顺手看见。

branches.en: THE PRACTICAL CHOICE: policies and business options weighed on one sheet before a decision.
branches.cn: 实务上的取舍：政策与商业备选方案在决策前放到一张表上称量。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION AND THE PERIOD: legal codes compared, and historical cases set beside each other.
branches.cn: 制度与时期：法典被对照，历史案例被并置。

branches.en: THE LITERARY COMPARISON: two traditions read against each other so that conventions show.
branches.cn: 文学比较：两个传统互相映照，使成规显形。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: groups and cohorts compared with data rather than with impression.
branches.cn: 数字：用数据而非印象比较组别与队列。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin comparative adjective and a Greek noun of breaking up, both still productive in English.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁的比较形容词与希腊的拆解名词合在一起，两者在英语中仍有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Comparare supplies the first half; analyein supplies the second, through Latin and French forms.
latinIntro.cn: 前半出自 comparare，后半出自 analyein，经由拉丁与法语形态进入英语。

items.meaning: a study by comparison of cases
items.meaningCN: 通过比较案例所作的研究
items.example: The phrase is a fixed research term.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是固定的研究术语。

items.example: It gives the first half its pairing sense.
items.exampleCN: 它给前半部分配对之意。

items.example: It also builds prepare and repair.
items.exampleCN: 它还构成 prepare 与 repair。

items.example: It turns comparare into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把 comparare 变成形容词。

items.example: It gives analysis the sense of taking apart thoroughly.
items.exampleCN: 它给 analysis 彻底拆解之意。

items.example: The root supplies the image of loosening a knot.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供解开绳结的意象。

items.example: It builds analysis, synthesis and diagnosis.
items.exampleCN: 它构成分析、综合与诊断等词。
它从 analysis 造出 analytical。

items.example: It builds analyst, the person who does the work.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 analyst，指做这项工作的人。

latinEntries.example: The verb supplies the comparing half of the term.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词提供该术语中「比较」那一半。

latinEntries.meaning: a loosening; a resolving into parts
latinEntries.example: Greek analysis means a loosening up, a resolving into parts.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 analysis 意为松开，即拆解为部分。

latinEntries.example: Greek lyein means to loosen, and gives -lysis in English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 lyein 意为松开，并给出英语的 -lysis。

definition_zh: 温度波动；温度在某段时间内围绕基准值上下起伏的现象
definition_en: the rise and fall of temperature around a baseline over a period of time
core_image: 恒温箱的记录纸上，一条锯齿线始终围着平直的基准线上下抖动
scene: 实验室的恒温箱前，技术员盯着记录纸上的锯齿线，那条线始终围着一条平直的基准线上下抖动。 The chart showed a small temperature fluctuation around the set point.
sceneCN: 这里指受控设备中围绕设定值的温度波动（第 5 个义项：恒温系统内的温度起伏）；句意为记录图显示设定点附近有小幅温度波动。图中可辨识物件：恒温箱、记录纸、锯齿曲线、基准线。

pos.zh: 名词短语：可数，指一次或一段温度起伏；常带表示幅度的介词短语

collocations.phrase: a temperature fluctuation of two degrees

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语表示「调和、适度」的动词派生，义为「温度」
由拉丁语表示「波动」的动词构成，义为「起伏；波动」
由动词加表示「作用、过程」的词尾构成，义为「波动」
由动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「起伏不定的」
与本短语第一成分同源，义为「温和的；温带的」

senses.title: Rise and fall around a baseline
senses.definition: the general movement of temperature up and down rather than in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 温度上下往复而非单向变化的总体运动
senses.example: A temperature fluctuation of two degrees was enough to change the reaction rate.
senses.exampleCN: 两度的温度波动就足以改变反应速率。
senses.why: Change can be directional or oscillating, and this phrase names the oscillating kind.
senses.whyCN: 变化可以是单向的，也可以是往复的，这个短语命名的是往复的那一类。

senses.title: Short-term wobble versus trend
senses.definition: a brief departure from the average that carries little information about the long run
senses.definitionCN: 对平均值的短暂偏离，对长期走势几乎不提供信息
senses.example: A single temperature fluctuation says little about a long-term trend.
senses.exampleCN: 单次温度波动对长期趋势说明不了什么。
senses.why: Mixing up a wiggle with a slope is one of the commonest mistakes in reading data.
senses.whyCN: 把一次抖动当成一段斜坡，是读数据时最常见的错误之一。

senses.title: Diurnal fluctuation
senses.definition: the daily cycle of warming by day and cooling by night
senses.definitionCN: 白天升温、夜间降温的每日循环
senses.example: Diurnal temperature fluctuation is largest under clear skies and dry air.
senses.exampleCN: 晴朗干燥的空气下，昼夜温度波动最大。
senses.why: Sunlight arrives and leaves on a schedule, so the temperature follows a daily rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 阳光按时间表到来与离开，温度便随之有每日的节律。

senses.title: Seasonal fluctuation
senses.definition: the yearly swing between warm and cold seasons
senses.definitionCN: 一年之中暖季与冷季之间的摆动
senses.example: Seasonal temperature fluctuation drives the timing of migration.
senses.exampleCN: 季节温度波动决定迁徙的时间。
senses.why: The planet's tilt imposes a yearly wave, and living things read that wave as a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 行星的倾斜造成一年的波，生物把这列波读成日历。

senses.title: Fluctuation in a controlled system
senses.titleCN: 受控系统中的温度波动
senses.definition: the small deviation from a set point inside an oven, incubator or reactor
senses.definitionCN: 烤箱、培养箱或反应器内偏离设定值的小幅偏差
senses.example: The incubator keeps temperature fluctuation below a tenth of a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这台培养箱把温度波动控制在十分之一度以内。
senses.why: Control engineering cares about the size of the wiggle, not the average alone.
senses.whyCN: 控制工程关心抖动的幅度，而不只是平均值。

senses.title: Fluctuation in climate records
senses.titleCN: 气候记录中的温度波动
senses.definition: a multi-year or multi-century rise and fall recovered from proxies and instruments
senses.definitionCN: 从代用资料与仪器中复原的多年或数百年尺度的升降
senses.example: Proxy records reveal a temperature fluctuation that lasted several centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 代用资料揭示了一次持续数百年的温度波动。
senses.why: Past climates are read as waves, so the phrase describes the shape rather than a single value.
senses.whyCN: 过去的气候被读成波，因此这个短语描述的是形状而非单个数值。

senses.title: Statistical fluctuation
senses.definition: variation that comes from random sampling rather than from a real physical change
senses.definitionCN: 源于随机抽样而非真实物理变化的变化
senses.example: Some of the variation is just statistical temperature fluctuation, not a real signal.
senses.exampleCN: 其中一部分变化只是统计上的温度涨落，并非真实信号。
senses.why: Randomness alone can produce wiggles, so a signal has to rise above the noise.
senses.whyCN: 随机性本身就能制造抖动，因此信号必须高出噪声。

senses.title: Body temperature fluctuation
senses.definition: the normal or abnormal daily variation in the temperature of a living body
senses.definitionCN: 活体温度的正常或异常日常变化
senses.example: A temperature fluctuation of half a degree can signal an infection.
senses.exampleCN: 半度的体温波动就可能提示感染。
senses.why: Physiology uses a narrow band, so even a small wiggle becomes clinically meaningful.
senses.whyCN: 生理学的带宽很窄，因此即使很小的抖动也具有临床意义。

senses.title: Ocean temperature fluctuation
senses.definition: the rise and fall of sea surface temperature that buoys and satellites track
senses.definitionCN: 浮标与卫星所追踪的海表温度升降
senses.example: Ocean temperature fluctuation on the equator is what the buoys are built to track.
senses.exampleCN: 赤道上的海温波动正是这些浮标被造出来追踪的对象。
senses.why: The ocean stores and releases heat slowly, so its wiggles run on longer periods than air.
senses.whyCN: 海洋缓慢地储存与释放热量，因此它的波动周期比空气更长。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun for a moderate mixture with a Latin noun for wave motion. Both roots are well documented; the phrase itself was assembled in scientific writing, so its first appearance is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表示「适度调和」的拉丁名词，与一个表示波浪运动的拉丁名词组合起来。两个词根来源有据；短语本身是在科学写作中组合而成的，首次出现只有约数。

items.en: Temperare meant to mix in due proportion or to moderate.
items.cn: 这个动词表示按适当比例混合或使之适度。

items.en: The noun named a balanced mixture and later the moderate state of the air.
items.cn: 这个名词指调和的比例，后指空气的适中状态。

items.en: English shifted the noun from balance to the degree of heat measured by a scale.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词从「平衡」转到用刻度测量的热度。

items.en: Fluctus meant a wave on water, from the verb for flowing.
items.cn: 这个词表示水面上的波浪，来自表示「流动」的动词。

items.en: The verb meant to move like a wave, to rise and fall, to waver.
items.cn: 这个动词表示像波浪一样运动、上下起伏、摇摆。

items.en: Scientific writing joined the two nouns to name heat that will not hold still.
items.cn: 科学写作把两个名词连在一起，命名不肯静止的热度。

note.en: The first group shares the word temperature but names different features of it; the second group names other kinds of up-and-down movement.
note.cn: 第一组共享「温度」一词但指它的不同特征；第二组指其他上下起伏的运动。

entries.definition: The rate at which temperature changes with distance.
entries.definitionCN: 温度随距离变化的速率。

entries.definition: A layer where temperature rises with height instead of falling.
entries.definitionCN: 温度随高度上升而非下降的一层大气。

entries.definition: The departure of temperature from a long-term average.
entries.definitionCN: 温度对长期平均值的偏离。

entries.definition: The span between the highest and lowest values.
entries.definitionCN: 最高值与最低值之间的跨度。

entries.definition: A device that converts heat into a reading.
entries.definitionCN: 把热量转换为读数的装置。

entries.definition: A change in amount or level.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或水平的变化。

entries.definition: A regular back-and-forth movement.
entries.definitionCN: 有规律的往复运动。

entries.definition: A large movement from one extreme to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个极端到另一端的大幅移动。

entries.definition: A departure from a standard or expected value.
entries.definitionCN: 对标准或预期值的偏离。

entries.definition: Random variation that obscures a signal.
entries.definitionCN: 掩盖信号的随机变化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow one line on a chart as it wiggle around a straight reference; abstract ones treat fluctuation as information that must be separated from trend and noise.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想跟随图上一条围着直线抖动的曲线；抽象联想把波动看作必须与趋势、噪声分开的信息。

normal.en: A recorder draws a sawtooth around a straight set line.
normal.cn: 记录仪在平直的设定线周围画出锯齿。

normal.en: At dawn the line climbs, at night it falls, and that is the daily wiggle.
normal.cn: 黎明曲线上升，夜里下降，那就是每日的抖动。

normal.en: A summer and winter swing is just the same wiggle at a slower tempo.
normal.cn: 夏冬之间的摆动只是同一抖动放慢了节奏。

normal.en: A good oven keeps its wiggle smaller than a tenth of a degree.
normal.cn: 好的烤箱把抖动控制在十分之一度以内。

normal.en: Buoys watch the same wiggle on the surface of the ocean.
normal.cn: 浮标在海洋表面观察同一种抖动。

abstract.en: Fluctuation is a wave in a number, not necessarily a wave in the world.
abstract.cn: 波动是数字里的波，未必是世界里的波。

abstract.en: Before calling a wiggle a trend, ask how long the record is.
abstract.cn: 把抖动称为趋势之前，先问记录有多长。

abstract.en: Every measurement carries a small tremble that belongs to the instrument, not the object.
abstract.cn: 每个测量都带着一点颤抖，那属于仪器而不属于对象。

examples.en: The reactor is designed to tolerate a small temperature fluctuation.
examples.cn: 该反应堆被设计成能承受小幅温度波动。

examples.en: Scientists separated the long-term trend from yearly temperature fluctuation.
examples.cn: 科学家把长期趋势与逐年温度波动分开。

examples.en: A sudden temperature fluctuation cracked the glass.
examples.cn: 一次突然的温度波动使玻璃裂了。

dict_mnemonic.text: temperature（温度）+ fluctuation（波动）——温度的上下起伏，即温度波动

root: 由 temperature 与 fluctuation 组合。前者源自拉丁语 temperatura「调和的比例」，出自 temperare「调和、使适度」；后者源自拉丁语 fluctus「波浪」及其动词 fluctuare「起伏摇摆」，与表示「流动」的词根相关。短语在科学写作中组合而成，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses take one wiggle and read it at different scales: around a baseline, against a trend, across a day, a season, a machine, a century, a sample, a body and an ocean.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项拿同一次抖动在不同尺度上解读：围绕基准、对照趋势、跨一天、跨一季、在一台设备里、跨一个世纪、在一个样本里、在一具身体里与在一片海洋上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sawtooth line hugging a straight reference line on recorder paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：记录纸上贴着直线基准的锯齿曲线。

branches.en: THE CORE: up-and-down motion, and the warning not to mistake it for a slope.
branches.cn: 核心：上下往复的运动，以及不要把它误认成斜坡的提醒。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR SCALES: one turn of the earth and one turn of the year.
branches.cn: 日历尺度：地球自转一圈与一年一圈。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: a set point and the small deviation allowed around it.
branches.cn: 机器：一个设定点，以及允许其周围的小偏差。

branches.en: THE LONG RECORD AND THE SAMPLE: centuries recovered from proxies, and randomness inside a measurement.
branches.cn: 长记录与样本：从代用资料复原的数百年，以及测量内部的随机性。

branches.en: THE TWO BODIES: a narrow physiological band and the slow heat of the sea.
branches.cn: 两个躯体：狭窄的生理带宽与海洋缓慢的热量。

intro.en: Two Latin roots, one of moderation and one of waves, supply both halves of the phrase.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁词根，一个表示「调和」，一个表示「波浪」，提供了短语的两半。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies temperare and its noun for balanced heat, then fluctus and its verb for wave motion; English adds the noun endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示调和及其名词，以及表示波浪的名词与动词；英语加上名词词尾。

items.example: The idea of balance is older than the idea of heat.
items.exampleCN: 「平衡」的观念比「热度」的观念更古老。

items.example: The noun moved from mixture to the state of the air.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从「混合比例」转到空气的状态。

items.example: It forms the English noun for the measured state.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示被测状态的英语名词。

items.example: It is the root of all the wave words in the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是短语中所有「波」类词的根。

items.example: The verb describes motion that will not settle.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述不肯安定下来的运动。

items.example: It turns the verb into the name of the movement.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成该运动的名称。

items.example: The first half of the phrase names what is moving.
items.exampleCN: 短语的前半命名了在动的东西。

items.example: The second half names how it moves.
items.exampleCN: 短语的后半命名了它如何动。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语表示「调和、适度」的动词派生，义为「温度」
由拉丁语表示「波动」的动词构成，义为「起伏；波动」
由动词加表示「作用、过程」的词尾构成，义为「波动」
由动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「起伏不定的」
与本短语第一成分同源，义为「温和的；温带的」

definition_zh: 兴高采烈；提升；赞扬
definition_en: a feeling of great joy, or the act of raising someone in rank or praising them highly
core_image: 两双手把一个人高高举起，众人都要仰头看
scene: 毕业典礼上，她把帽子抛向空中，脸上全是压不住的狂喜。 A wave of exaltation swept over the graduates as the music began.
sceneCN: 这里 exaltation 是「兴高采烈、狂喜」（第 1 个义项：情绪被举高）；句意：音乐响起时，一阵狂喜掠过毕业生们。

pos.zh: 兴高采烈；提升；赞扬

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀 -ation 还原的动词，义为「提升；颂扬；使兴奋」
动词加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「地位高的；崇高的；兴奋的」
动词加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「令人振奋的；使人高尚的」

senses.title: A feeling of intense joy
senses.definition: a feeling of great joy and excitement that lifts the mind above its ordinary mood
senses.definitionCN: 极度喜悦与兴奋，心神被抬到日常情绪之上
senses.example: A sense of exaltation filled the hall as the choir rose.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团起立时，一种狂喜充满了大厅。
senses.why: Latin altus means high, so a lifted mind is the source image, and the noun names that upward surge of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 altus 意为「高」，心神被举高正是这个词的画面来源，名词便指情绪向上涌起的状态。

senses.title: The act of raising to a high rank
senses.definition: the act of raising a person to a higher position, honour, or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 把人提升到更高职位、荣誉或地位的行为
senses.example: His exaltation to the chairmanship surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他被擢升为主席，谁也不感到意外。
senses.why: The verb exaltare means literally to lift up, so applied to persons the noun names the act of placing someone on higher ground.
senses.whyCN: 动词 exaltare 字面就是「举起来」，用在人身上，名词便指把人放到更高位置的这个动作。

senses.title: Praise or glorification
senses.definition: the act of praising someone or something highly, especially in worship
senses.definitionCN: 高度赞扬某人或某物，尤指在宗教崇拜中
senses.example: The psalm ends in the exaltation of the divine name.
senses.exampleCN: 这首圣诗以颂扬神名作结。
senses.why: To lift a name up in words is to praise it, so the same upward image moved from physical height into speech and worship.
senses.whyCN: 用言语把名字举高就是颂扬，同一个「向上」的意象于是从身体的高度转移到言说与崇拜里。

senses.title: A state of lofty dignity
senses.definition: the condition of being elevated in dignity, purity, or spiritual worth
senses.definitionCN: 在尊严、纯净或精神价值上处于高处的状态
senses.example: The old hymns speak of the exaltation of the soul after death.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的赞美诗谈到灵魂在死后得到的升华。
senses.why: Because height was read as worth, the noun also names a lasting elevated condition rather than a single act or a passing feeling.
senses.whyCN: 因为「高」被读作「贵」，这个名词也指一种持久的高贵状态，而不只是一次举动或一阵情绪。

intro.en: Exaltation comes from Latin altus, high, through the verb exaltare, to lift up.
intro.cn: exaltation 源自拉丁语 altus（高），经由动词 exaltare（举高）而来。

items.en: Altus means high or lofty, and is generally taken as growing from alere, to nourish, in the sense of grown tall.
items.cn: altus 意为高的、崇高的，一般认为它源自 alere（养育），取「已经长高」之意。

items.en: The verb exaltare joins ex- to altus and means to lift up or to raise.
items.cn: 动词 exaltare 由 ex- 与 altus 合成，意为举起、抬高。

items.en: The noun exaltatio names a lifting up, whether of a body, a rank, or a mood.
items.cn: 名词 exaltatio 指举起，可以是身体、地位或情绪上的举起。

items.en: Old French exaltation keeps both the religious and the social senses alive.
items.cn: 古法语 exaltation 同时让宗教与社会两方面的含义延续下来。

items.en: English adopts the word for raising in rank, for praise, and for lifted feeling.
items.cn: 英语采用这个词，用来表示提升地位、颂扬与情绪高涨。

items.en: In modern use the emotional sense of elation is the most common one.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，表示情绪高涨的「狂喜」义最为常见。

note.en: Exaltation belongs to the high family of altus, beside the verb exalt, and near the words for joy, raising, and praise.
note.cn: exaltation 属于 altus 的「高」词族，与动词 exalt 同根，并与表示喜悦、提升、赞扬的词相邻。

entries.definition: to raise in rank or to praise highly
entries.definitionCN: 提升地位；高度颂扬

entries.definition: high in rank, noble, or filled with joy
entries.definitionCN: 地位高的；崇高的；满心欢喜的

entries.definition: great rejoicing and triumph
entries.definitionCN: 欢腾与得意——与 exaltation 只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自 exsultare「跳起」）

entries.definition: a mood of high spirits and joy
entries.definitionCN: 情绪高涨；欢欣鼓舞

entries.definition: the act of raising something or the state of being raised
entries.definitionCN: 提升；被抬起的状态

entries.definition: the act of praising something as glorious
entries.definitionCN: 颂扬；把某物赞为荣耀

normalIntro.en: Exaltation carries the Latin altus, high: something in the mind or in rank has been lifted.
normalIntro.cn: exaltation 带着拉丁语 altus（高）的底子：不是心神被举高，就是地位被举高。

normal.en: Exalt and exaltation share the Latin altus, which means high.
normal.cn: exalt 与 exaltation 共享拉丁语 altus，意为「高」。

normal.en: Altitude comes from the same altus, so height ties the whole family together.
normal.cn: altitude 也来自同一个 altus，高度把整个词族串在一起。

normal.en: Exultation looks alike but comes from exsultare, to leap up.
normal.cn: exultation 形似，却来自 exsultare（跳起来）。

normal.en: In worship, exaltation names the lifting of a name in praise.
normal.cn: 在崇拜中，exaltation 指把某个名字高举颂扬。

normal.en: Raise is the plain verb, while exalt is the literary and religious one.
normal.cn: raise 是平实的动词，exalt 则更文学、更宗教。

abstract.en: Picture a kite pulled up by a gust until it rides above the rooftops.
abstract.cn: 想象风筝被一阵风拉起，一直升到屋顶之上。

abstract.en: See a hand lifting a young scholar onto a higher step of a stone stair.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把年轻学者托上石阶更高的一级。

abstract.en: Hear a crowd lift one name high above all the noise.
abstract.cn: 想象人群把一个名字高高举过所有喧哗。

examples.en: The crowd rose in a mood of pure exaltation.
examples.cn: 人群起身，沉浸在纯粹的狂喜之中。

examples.en: His exaltation to the rank of master came after thirty years of service.
examples.cn: 在服务三十年后，他被擢升为大师。

examples.en: The hymn is a song of exaltation, not of complaint.
examples.cn: 这首圣诗是一曲颂扬，而不是抱怨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱个高台」——读起来像「爱个高台」，人往高台上一站，心就飘起来，既是被提升也是狂喜；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、向上）+ altus（高，一般认为源自 alere「养育、长高」）→ 动词 exaltare（举高、抬高）→ 名词 exaltatio → 英语 exaltation，核心义「把人或心举到高处」。

sensesIntro.en: Exaltation moves from a lifted feeling of joy, to the act of raising someone in rank, to praise, and finally to a lasting state of lofty dignity.
sensesIntro.cn: exaltation 从被举高的喜悦，走到把某人提升的举动，再到颂扬，最后指一种持久的高贵状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands lifting a person until the crowd must look up.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双手把一个人举起，众人只能抬头看。

branches.en: Joy is the mind lifted above its usual level.
branches.cn: 喜悦就是心神被举到平常水平之上。

branches.en: Rank is the body placed on a higher step.
branches.cn: 地位就是把身体放上更高的一级台阶。

branches.en: Praise is a name lifted in speech and song.
branches.cn: 赞扬就是在言说与歌唱里把名字举高。

branches.en: Dignity is height that has become permanent.
branches.cn: 高贵是被固定下来的高度。

branches.en: Singing praise often produces the lifted feeling itself.
branches.cn: 唱颂本身常常就会带来那种被举起的感觉。

intro.en: Exaltation combines the Latin prefix ex-, the root altus, high, and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: exaltation 由拉丁语前缀 ex-、词根 altus（高）与名词后缀 -ation 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin altus means high or deep, and exaltare means to raise or to lift up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 altus 意为高的、深的，exaltare 意为举高、抬高。

items.example: The prefix ex- turns height into a lifting.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把「高」变成了「举起」。
altus 描述高耸挺立之物。

items.example: Altus is generally taken to grow from alere.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为 altus 源自 alere。
exaltare 由 ex- 与 altus 合成。

items.example: Exaltatio is the Latin action noun.
items.exampleCN: exaltatio 是拉丁语的动作名词。

items.example: The suffix -ation builds a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Exalt is the shorter English verb.
items.exampleCN: exalt 是更简短的英语动词。

items.example: Exultation comes from exsultare, to leap up.

definition_zh: 化学键；把原子结合在一起的作用力
definition_en: the force that holds atoms together in a molecule, crystal or compound
core_image: 两个小球之间一根被拉紧的短杆，把两端固定成一个整体
scene: 两个小球之间一根被拉紧的短杆，把两端固定成一个整体。 A chemical bond holds the two atoms together in the molecule.
sceneCN: 这里 chemical bond 指把原子维系在一起的作用力（第 1 个义项：原子间形成稳定连接的力量）；句意：一条化学键把分子中的两个原子结合在一起。图中可辨识物件：两个小球、短杆、绷紧的连线、整体支架。

pos.zh: 化学键；原子间的结合力

senses.title: The force holding atoms together
senses.titleCN: 把原子维系在一起的作用力
senses.definition: the attraction that keeps atoms joined in a stable arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 使原子保持在稳定排布中的吸引力
senses.example: A chemical bond holds the two atoms together in the molecule.
senses.exampleCN: 一条化学键把分子中的两个原子结合在一起。
senses.why: the phrase names the tie itself, the thing that remains while the atoms stay put.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语命名的正是那条纽带，即在原子不动时仍然存在的那个东西。

senses.title: A covalent bond
senses.definition: a bond formed by two atoms sharing a pair of electrons
senses.definitionCN: 两个原子共享一对电子而形成的键
senses.example: Each covalent chemical bond in methane shares one pair of electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 甲烷中的每条共价键共享一对电子。
senses.why: the general phrase narrows by qualifier, and the shared-electron case is the commonest one taught first.
senses.whyCN: 通称靠限定词收窄，而共享电子这一情形是最先教授、也最常见的一种。

senses.title: An ionic bond
senses.definition: a bond formed by the attraction between oppositely charged ions
senses.definitionCN: 由带相反电荷的离子相互吸引而形成的键
senses.example: The ionic chemical bond in salt breaks when the crystal dissolves.
senses.exampleCN: 盐中的离子键在晶体溶解时断开。
senses.why: when electrons are transferred rather than shared, the resulting attraction is still called a bond, so the phrase covers it.
senses.whyCN: 当电子被转移而非共享时，由此产生的吸引仍被称为键，因此这个短语也涵盖它。

senses.title: A metallic bond
senses.definition: a bond in which metal cations are held by a shared sea of electrons
senses.definitionCN: 金属阳离子被共享的电子海维系的键
senses.example: A metallic chemical bond lets the metal bend without breaking.
senses.exampleCN: 金属键使金属可以弯曲而不断裂。
senses.why: metals need a third model, and the general phrase with a qualifier carries it like the other two.
senses.whyCN: 金属需要第三种模型，带限定词的通称像前两种一样承载它。

senses.title: A hydrogen bond
senses.definition: a weak attraction between a hydrogen atom and a nearby electronegative atom
senses.definitionCN: 氢原子与邻近电负性原子之间的弱吸引
senses.example: A hydrogen chemical bond between the strands is weak but numerous.
senses.exampleCN: 两条链之间的氢键虽弱，数量却多。
senses.why: weaker links are still called bonds in chemistry, and the qualifier keeps them distinct from the strong kinds.
senses.whyCN: 较弱的连接在化学中仍称键，限定词使它们与强键区分开。

senses.title: The drawn line for a bond
senses.titleCN: 结构式中表示键的短线
senses.definition: the short line in a structural formula that stands for a bond
senses.definitionCN: 结构式中代表一条键的短线
senses.example: A double chemical bond is drawn as two short parallel lines.
senses.exampleCN: 双键画成两条平行的短线。
senses.why: the mark takes the name of the thing it marks, a familiar shift from object to symbol.
senses.whyCN: 标记取用了被标记之物的名字，这是从实物到符号的常见转义。

senses.title: Bond length and energy as properties
senses.definition: the measurable features of a bond, such as its length, strength and energy
senses.definitionCN: 键可测量的特征，如长度、强度与能量
senses.example: The chemical bond energy tells you how much heat is released.
senses.exampleCN: 化学键能告诉你释放了多少热。
senses.why: once a bond is treated as an object, it can be measured, and the phrase then carries those measurements.
senses.whyCN: 一旦键被当作对象，它就可以被测量，这个短语于是承载这些测量值。

senses.title: A strong tie between people
senses.titleCN: 比喻：人与人之间牢固的联结
senses.definition: figuratively, a strong and hard-to-break connection between people
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指人与人之间牢固、难以拆开的联系
senses.example: Years of shared work formed a chemical bond between the two researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 多年共事在两位研究者之间形成了一种牢固的联结。
senses.why: the metaphor works because a chemical bond is exactly what is hard to break, a usage that remains clearly figurative.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻之所以成立，正因为化学键恰恰是难以拆断的东西；此用法仍明显是比喻。

intro.en: The phrase joins chemical, which descends through Medieval Latin from the alchemy word, and bond, a Norse noun meaning a cord. The two halves have different origins. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把 chemical（经中世纪拉丁语上溯炼金术一词）与 bond（意为绳索的诺斯语名词）组合起来。两半来源不同。年代均为约数。

items.en: Chemical descends from Medieval Latin chymicus and alchimia, the alchemy word of disputed pre-Greek origin.
items.cn: chemical 上溯中世纪拉丁语 chymicus 与 alchimia，即那个希腊语之前来源有争议的炼金术词。

items.en: Bond comes from Old Norse band, a cord or shackle, and is related to English bind; it has no Latin ancestor.
items.cn: bond 出自古诺斯语 band「绳、镣铐」，与英语 bind 同族；它没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: English bond first named a restraint and then a promise sealed by one, which is how the financial sense arose.
items.cn: 英语 bond 先指束缚，再指以此封存的承诺，金融义即由此而来。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemists spoke of the bond between atoms once valence theory showed that atoms combine in fixed ratios.
items.cn: 当价键理论表明原子按固定比例结合后，19 世纪的化学家开始谈论原子之间的键。

items.en: Twentieth-century quantum chemistry sorted bonds into covalent, ionic, metallic and weak kinds, all still called chemical bonds.
items.cn: 20 世纪的量子化学把键分为共价、离子、金属与弱作用等类型，它们仍统称化学键。

items.en: Source uncertain (half of the phrase): the deeper origin of the alchemy word behind chemical is disputed, while bond is securely Germanic; only the first half carries this uncertainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（短语的一半）：chemical 背后那个炼金术词的更深来源有争议，而 bond 确属日耳曼语；这种不确定性只在短语的前一半。

note.en: The first group is the bond family in its other shapes; the second group names related links and the general idea of attraction.
note.cn: 第一组是 bond 词族的其他形态；第二组是相关的连接说法与「吸引」这一总体概念。

entries.definition: The bare noun can mean a tie between people, a financial instrument or a bond between atoms; chemical narrows it.
entries.definitionCN: 不带限定的名词可指人际纽带、金融债券或原子间的键；chemical 使它收窄。

entries.definition: The forming of bonds; the chemical bond is the link that results, not the activity of making it.
entries.definitionCN: 指成键的过程；化学键是形成后的连接，而不是形成这一活动。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun of chemistry; on its own it says nothing about a tie between atoms.
entries.definitionCN: 化学的形容词与名词；单独使用不涉及原子间的连接。

entries.definition: The adverb of viewpoint or method; it cannot replace the noun phrase in a sentence about atoms.
entries.definitionCN: 表示视角或方法的副词；在谈论原子的句子里不能替代这个名词短语。

entries.definition: The general pull between particles; a bond is the stable result of that pull, not the pull itself.
entries.definitionCN: 粒子间一般的拉力；键是这种拉力稳定后的结果，而非拉力本身。

entries.definition: A connection between parts; in chemistry it often names how groups are joined, rather than the force.
entries.definitionCN: 部件之间的连接；在化学中常指基团如何相连，而非那股力。

entries.definition: A measurable push or pull; a bond involves forces but is named as the link, not as the force value.
entries.definitionCN: 可测量的推或拉；键涉及力，但命名的是连接，不是力的数值。

entries.definition: The holding together of like molecules by weak attraction; it is not a bond between two atoms in a molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 同类分子靠弱吸引聚拢；它不是分子内两原子之间的键。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real source lines, the real word family and real textbook phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两条真实的来源线、真实的同族词与真实的教科书说法。

normal.en: Chemical is the adjective of chemistry; bond is a cord. Together they name the cord between atoms.
normal.cn: chemical 是化学的形容词，bond 是一根绳；合起来就是原子之间的那根绳。

normal.en: The family runs bond, bonding, bonded, chemical and chemistry.
normal.cn: 同族词有 bond、bonding、bonded、chemical 与 chemistry。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the measurements: bond length, bond energy, bond type.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出测量项：键长、键能、键型。

normal.en: Qualifiers do the sorting: covalent, ionic, metallic and hydrogen bonds.
normal.cn: 限定词负责分类：共价键、离子键、金属键、氢键。

normal.en: Breaking a bond costs energy; forming one releases it, which is why bond energy is always discussed with heat.
normal.cn: 断键要耗能，成键会放能，所以键能总与热一起讨论。

abstract.en: Picture two beads held apart by a taut rod that neither can escape.
abstract.cn: 想象两颗珠子被一根绷紧的短杆撑住，谁也逃不开。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn between two dots on a page, standing for a force nobody can see.
abstract.cn: 想象纸上两点之间画的一条线，代表一股谁也看不见的力。

abstract.en: Picture two colleagues who finish each other's sentences after years of work.
abstract.cn: 想象两位同事多年共事后，能接上对方没说完的话。

examples.en: The chemical bond in nitrogen is strong enough to make the gas inert.
examples.cn: 氮气中的化学键足够强，使这种气体不活泼。

examples.en: Ultraviolet light can break a chemical bond in the pigment.
examples.cn: 紫外光能断开颜料中的一条化学键。

examples.en: Students drew every chemical bond in the formula before naming the shape.
examples.cn: 学生们先画出式中每条化学键，再给形状命名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「chemical（化学的）+ bond（纽带）」——原子之间那条化学的绳 → 化学键

root: chemical 上溯中世纪拉丁 chymicus / alchimia（炼金术词，希腊语之前来源有争议）；bond 出自古诺斯语 band「绳、镣铐」，与 bind 同族，无拉丁祖先。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one link: two atoms are tied together. The link is then sorted into shared-electron, transferred-electron, metallic and weak kinds, drawn as a line, measured as energy, and finally borrowed for a human tie.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条连接展开：两个原子被系在一起。这条连接随后分为共享电子、转移电子、金属与弱作用等类型，被画成一条线、被测量为能量，最后借用于人与人之间的纽带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two beads fixed at either end of a taut rod, one whole instead of two parts.
core.cn: 核心意象：两颗珠子固定在绷紧短杆的两端，成为一体而非两件。

branches.en: THE TIE ITSELF: whatever keeps the atoms in place once they are joined.
branches.cn: 纽带本身：原子结合之后使它们留在原位的那个东西。

branches.en: SHARED OR TRANSFERRED: electrons either travel together or move across.
branches.cn: 共享或转移：电子要么同行，要么换边。

branches.en: SEA AND GLUE: a metal holds its ions in a shared sea, while a hydrogen link is weak but numerous.
branches.cn: 电子海与胶水：金属把离子浸在共享的电子海里，氢键则弱而多。

branches.en: PICTURE AND NUMBER: a line on the page, and a length or energy to measure.
branches.cn: 图与数：纸上的一条线，以及可测量的长度或能量。

branches.en: HUMAN TIE: the same word for a friendship that is hard to break.
branches.cn: 人的纽带：同一个词也用于难以拆断的友谊。

intro.en: The phrase is half borrowed Latin and half Germanic: an adjective of the chemistry family in front, a Norse noun behind.
intro.cn: 这个短语一半是借入的拉丁语，一半是日耳曼语：前面是化学词族的形容词，后面是诺斯语名词。

latinIntro.en: Only the first half has Latin entries, through chymicus and alchimia; bond itself is Germanic and has none.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前一半有拉丁词条，经 chymicus 与 alchimia；bond 本身属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词条。

items.example: The stem serves the whole chemistry family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干服务整个化学词族。

items.example: The ending makes chemical an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 chemical 变成形容词。

items.example: A chemical bond is a link studied by chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 化学键是化学研究的一种连接。

items.example: Bond is the noun that carries the image of a cord.
items.exampleCN: bond 是承载绳索意象的那个名词。

items.example: A chemical bond holds the atoms together.
items.exampleCN: 化学键把原子维系在一起。

items.example: Bonded atoms sit at fixed distances.
items.exampleCN: 成键的原子保持固定距离。

items.example: Bind and bond share a Germanic origin.
items.exampleCN: bind 与 bond 共享一个日耳曼语来源。

items.example: A binder keeps the powder in shape.
items.exampleCN: 黏合剂使粉末保持形状。

definition_zh: 转移（目光）；防止；避免（灾祸）
definition_en: to turn something away, especially the eyes or the face; also, to prevent something bad from happening
core_image: 危局袭来之前，一只手把目光和灾祸一同拨开
scene: 司机猛打方向盘，事故擦身而过。 Quick action averted a pileup on the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 avert 指「防止、避免」（第 2 个义项：使灾祸不发生）；句意：果断的处置避免了桥上的连环追尾。

pos.zh: 转移（目光等）；防止；避免

derivatives.zh: 厌恶；反感（avert 的名词同族）
厌恶的；不愿的（同族形容词）

senses.title: To turn the eyes or face away
senses.definition: to turn the eyes, gaze, or face away from something
senses.definitionCN: 把目光、视线或脸从某物上转开
senses.example: She averted her eyes during the accident scene.
senses.exampleCN: 事故场面出现时她移开了目光。
senses.why: The Latin root is literal here: ab, away, plus vertere, to turn.
senses.whyCN: 此处词根是字面的：ab「离开」+ vertere「转」。

senses.title: To prevent something bad
senses.definition: to stop an expected evil, harm, or crisis from happening
senses.definitionCN: 使预料中的灾祸、危害或危机不致发生
senses.example: Quiet diplomacy averted a trade war.
senses.exampleCN: 低调外交避免了一场贸易战。
senses.why: Turning the danger away extends the bodily motion to events.
senses.whyCN: 把危险「转」走，把身体动作延伸到了事件上。

senses.title: To deflect a course of events
senses.definition: to bend a process or trend off its path before it lands
senses.definitionCN: 在事态落定之前使其偏离原有轨道
senses.example: Reform averted the colony's slide into revolt.
senses.exampleCN: 改革使殖民地免于滑向叛乱。
senses.why: A trend is a moving thing; it too can be turned.
senses.whyCN: 趋势也是运动之物，同样可以被拨转。

senses.title: To ward off harm by ritual or custom
senses.definition: in traditional practice, to keep off evil through ritual means
senses.definitionCN: 传统习俗中通过仪式手段驱避灾厄
senses.example: Charms were nailed up to avert the evil eye.
senses.exampleCN: 人们钉上符咒以禳避邪眼。
senses.why: Before diplomacy there was magic: pushing evil aside with a gesture.
senses.whyCN: 在外交之前先是法术：用一个动作把邪祟推开。

senses.title: To divert resources or attention
senses.definition: to redirect money, effort, or attention elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 把资金、精力或注意力引向别处
senses.example: The agency averted funds to the flooded provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构把资金转拨给受涝省份。
senses.why: Whatever flows can be re-turned: water, cash, or care.
senses.whyCN: 凡流动之物皆可改道：水、资金、关怀皆然。

senses.title: To avoid by turning aside oneself
senses.definition: in older use, to step or lean aside to escape contact
senses.definitionCN: 旧式用法中侧身或俯身避开接触
senses.example: The fencer averted the thrust with a slip of the hip.
senses.exampleCN: 剑手侧髋一闪，避开了刺击。
senses.why: The earliest English sense kept the body at the center.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语义保留着身体中心。

senses.title: Averted, as a gaze or disaster
senses.titleCN: （分词用法）被移开的；被避免的
senses.definition: in participial use, describing a gaze held aside or a disaster just missed
senses.definitionCN: 分词用法，形容移开的视线或险些酿成的灾祸
senses.example: The report called it a narrowly averted meltdown.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称那是一次险些酿成的熔毁，幸被避免。
senses.why: The participle freezes the instant of successful turning.
senses.whyCN: 分词定格了「成功拨转」的一瞬。

senses.title: Averting, as a habit of the eyes
senses.definition: the gerundial use, habitual eye-avoidance in social behavior
senses.definitionCN: 动名词用法，指社交中习惯性的目光回避
senses.example: Constant averting of the gaze read as guilt.
senses.exampleCN: 频频回避目光被解读为心虚。
senses.why: A single motion, repeated, becomes a readable sign.
senses.whyCN: 单一动作不断重复，便成了可被解读的信号。

intro.en: Avert comes from Latin avertere, to turn away, from ab, away from, plus vertere, to turn; English borrowed the verb around the start of the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: avert 出自拉丁语 avertere「使转开」，由 ab（离开）+ vertere（转）构成；英语约在 15 世纪初借入该动词。

items.en: The turn-root descends from the reconstructed stem wer-, to bend or turn.
items.cn: 「转」词根出自重构词干 wer-「弯、转」。

items.en: averted was a common verb: to turn anything away, eyes, blows, omens.
items.cn: averted 是常用动词：目光、打击、凶兆皆可转开。

items.en: Roman religion spoke of averting omens, a divina ritu, ritual turning of fate.
items.cn: 罗马宗教有「以仪式禳解征兆」之说。

items.en: Middle English first used avert for physically turning aside.
items.cn: 中古英语先以 avert 表身体上的闪避。

items.en: The preventive sense hardened: to avert war, to avert ruin.
items.cn: 17 世纪「防止」义定型：avert war、avert ruin。

items.en: Today the two live senses are averted eyes and averted disaster.
items.cn: 如今该词的两个活跃义项是移开的目光与避免的灾难。

note.en: Group one gathers the vertere family and the eternal averse-adverse trap; group two gathers words of preventing and turning.
note.cn: 第一组收 vertere 词族与 averse-adverse 之辨；第二组收防止、转向义场的词。

entries.definition: adjective, unfavorable; adverse conditions work against you.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，不利的；adverse conditions 指不利条件，勿与 avert 混写。

entries.definition: the adjective of the same family: feeling turned away from something.
entries.definitionCN: 同族形容词：对某事心存厌恶。

entries.definition: to turn upside down; shares vertere.
entries.definitionCN: 倒转；同享 vertere 词根。

entries.definition: to stop something from happening; broader and blander than avert.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止发生；比 avert 更宽泛平直。

entries.definition: to act first so the bad thing cannot start.
entries.definitionCN: 先发制人地阻止，抢在坏事发生之前。

entries.definition: to turn aside a blow, question, or course.
entries.definitionCN: 使打击、问题或进程偏转。

entries.definition: to redirect a flow of things or attention.
entries.definitionCN: 使事物或注意力改道。

entries.definition: to move the body out of the way; informal and physical.
entries.definitionCN: 闪身躲避；口语且偏身体动作。

normalIntro.en: Read a-vert as away-turn: turn the eyes away, turn the disaster away.
normalIntro.cn: 把 a-vert 读作 away-turn：目光转走，灾难也转走。

normal.en: ab- away plus vert turn: the same vert as in reverse and convert.
normal.cn: ab- 离开 + vert 转：vert 与 reverse、convert 里的 vert 相同。

normal.en: avert one's eyes for the body sense; avert disaster for the event sense.
normal.cn: 身体义用 avert one's eyes，事件义用 avert disaster。

normal.en: Avert takes the danger as object, never the person as object.
normal.cn: avert 的宾语是危险本身，不是人。

normal.en: narrowly averted is the set news phrase for a near miss.
normal.cn: narrowly averted 是新闻固定说法：险些未能避免。

normal.en: Adverse is the adjective that got the d; avert lost it.
normal.cn: 带 d 的是形容词 adverse；avert 没有那个 d。

abstract.en: See a hand press the tiller just before the reef.
abstract.cn: 想象触礁前一只手按住了舵。

abstract.en: Avert is a small word for turning fate at the last second.
abstract.cn: avert 这么小的词，却在最后一秒拨转了命运。

abstract.en: Feel the neck pivot before the eyes do.
abstract.cn: 感觉脖颈先于眼睛转了过去。

examples.en: The pilot averted catastrophe with a textbook landing.
examples.cn: 飞行员以教科书式的降落避免了空难。

examples.en: He averted his gaze from the accident on the roadside.
examples.cn: 他移开视线，不去看路边的车祸。

examples.en: Talks averted a nationwide rail strike at the last hour.
examples.cn: 谈判在最后一刻避免了全国铁路大罢工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恶我特」——那锅汤端过来他就喊「恶我特」，赶紧把脸特特地转开

root: 出自拉丁语 avertere「使转开」，由 ab-（离开）+ vertere（转）构成，属 vertere 大词族（reverse、convert、divert 等同源）。约 15 世纪初进入中古英语，先表身体闪避，17 世纪起「防止灾祸」义成为主导。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn on one motion: the eyes averted, the disaster averted, the funds redirected, and the ritual gestures that once did the same work.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个动作展开：移开目光、拨开灾难、转拨资金，以及古时承担同样职能的禳解仪式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a firm hand turning eyes, then events, off their collision course.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手先把目光、再把事件从相撞的轨道上拨开。

branches.en: THE BODY SIDE: eyes, stances, and the habits they form.
branches.cn: 身体一面：目光、体态及其习惯。

branches.en: THE DISASTER SIDE: crises stopped and the participles that celebrate it.
branches.cn: 灾难一面：被阻止的危机及定格其成功的分词。

branches.en: THE TREND SIDE: histories bent before they break.
branches.cn: 趋势一面：在崩坏前被拨转的走向。

branches.en: THE RITUAL SIDE: charms and omens turned aside.
branches.cn: 仪式一面：被禳转的符咒与征兆。

branches.en: THE FLOW SIDE: money and attention given a new channel.
branches.cn: 流动一面：资金与注意力被引入新渠道。

intro.en: Avert is compact: prefix ab- plus stem vert, with no suffix left on the verb.
intro.cn: avert 结构紧凑：前缀 ab- 加词干 vert，动词本身不再带后缀。

latinIntro.en: The vertere stem generated dozens of English verbs and nouns through French -vert and -version forms.
latinIntro.cn: vertere 词干经法语 -vert、-version 形式繁衍出几十个英语动词和名词。

definition_zh: 风险管理；风险管控（识别、评估并降低损失可能性的系统做法）
definition_en: the systematic process of identifying, assessing and controlling the chance or impact of loss
core_image: 一张铺开的表格把每个可能出事的环节标成不同颜色，旁边一栏写着由谁去处理
scene: 暴雨将至，工地的安全主管把高空作业的吊篮全部收回，让班组改做室内检查。 Before the storm, the site's risk management team lowered every suspended platform and moved the crews indoors.
sceneCN: 这里指「把可能出事的环节先找出来并安排应对的整套做法」（第 1 个义项：系统地识别、评估并控制损失可能）；句意为暴雨前，工地的风险管理小组把所有悬吊平台降下，并把班组转到室内作业。可辨识物件：安全帽、气象雷达屏、吊篮、检查清单。

pos.zh: 风险管理（不可数，指一整套做法）
作定语：风险管理的（如风险管理框架）

forms.label: 动词短语（实施风险管理）

derivatives.zh: 由基础名词加表示执行者的复合成分 → 执行风险管理的人
短语的基础名词，本义「危险」→ 风险
基础名词加形容词后缀，义为「充满……」→ 有风险的
基础动词，借自意大利语「操控、驯马」→ 操控；管理
基础动词加名词后缀，义为「行为或群体」→ 管理；管理层
由「管理者」加形容词后缀，义为「属于……」→ 管理上的

senses.title: The systematic process of handling risk
senses.titleCN: 系统处理风险的全过程
senses.definition: the organized process of finding, measuring and reducing threats before they turn into losses
senses.definitionCN: 在威胁变成损失之前，有组织地发现、衡量并减少它的过程
senses.example: The plant's risk management begins with a walk-through of every production line.
senses.exampleCN: 该厂的风险管理从走遍每一条生产线开始。
senses.why: risk names the uncertain harm and management names the controlled handling, so the phrase is literally the handling of uncertain harm.
senses.whyCN: 风险指不确定的损害，管理指有控制的处理，连起来就是「对不确定损害的处理」。

senses.title: The department that runs it
senses.definition: the unit or team inside an organization that is responsible for the process
senses.definitionCN: 组织内部负责执行这一过程的部门或小组
senses.example: Risk management signed off on the new supplier after a credit check.
senses.exampleCN: 风险管理部门在信用审查后批准了这家新供应商。
senses.why: because the work is permanent, the phrase metonymically names the people and the office that carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 因为这项工作长期存在，整个短语便以转喻指执行它的人和部门。

senses.title: Market, credit and liquidity risk in finance
senses.titleCN: 金融领域的市场、信用与流动性风险
senses.definition: the practice of measuring and limiting the financial exposures of a bank or fund
senses.definitionCN: 衡量并限制银行或基金所承担金融敞口的做法
senses.example: Traders must keep their positions inside the limits set by risk management.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员必须把持仓保持在风险管理部门设定的限额之内。
senses.why: finance split the general idea into named exposures, so the phrase became a technical label for limits on money at risk.
senses.whyCN: 金融业把笼统的概念拆成有名目的敞口，这个短语于是成了「限定资金风险」的技术标签。

senses.title: Company-wide, or enterprise, risk
senses.titleCN: 覆盖整个企业的风险管理
senses.definition: a firm-wide view that compares and balances risks across all departments at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时比较并平衡各部门风险的全公司视角
senses.example: Enterprise risk management treats a supplier failure and a currency swing as one portfolio of threats.
senses.exampleCN: 企业风险管理把供应商断供与汇率波动当作同一组威胁来处理。
senses.why: once each department had its own risks, firms needed a level above them all, which is why enterprise was added to the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 各部门都有各自的风险之后，企业需要一个高于它们的层面，于是短语前加上了「企业」这一限定。

senses.title: Risk control on a project
senses.titleCN: 具体项目上的风险控制
senses.definition: the discipline of listing, ranking and answering threats to a project's cost, time and quality
senses.definitionCN: 列出、排序并回应项目成本、工期与质量所受威胁的做法
senses.example: The tunnel project keeps a risk register that is reviewed every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 这个隧道项目保留一份每周五复核的风险登记表。
senses.why: projects are temporary and each has its own deadline, so the same process is applied on a short horizon and called project risk management.
senses.whyCN: 项目是临时的，各有截止期限，同一套流程被放到短周期上使用，就称为项目风险管理。

senses.title: Transferring risk to an insurer
senses.definition: the use of insurance and contracts to move a loss to another party for a price
senses.definitionCN: 用保险与合同把损失以一定价格转移给另一方的做法
senses.example: Buying cover is risk management by transfer rather than by prevention.
senses.exampleCN: 购买保险属于以转移而非预防来进行的风险管理。
senses.why: the phrase covers not only reducing a threat but also deciding who should carry it, and insurance is the oldest such tool.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语不只包含减少威胁，也包含决定由谁承担，保险就是最古老的此类工具。

senses.title: Cyber and information risk
senses.titleCN: 网络与信息风险的管理
senses.definition: the protection of data and systems through access rules, backups and response drills
senses.definitionCN: 通过访问规则、备份与演练保护数据与系统的做法
senses.example: The hospital's risk management now includes phishing drills for every ward clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院的风险管理如今包括让每个病区文员参加钓鱼邮件演练。
senses.why: digital systems created a new class of loss that is cheap to prevent and expensive to suffer, so the same label was extended to them.
senses.whyCN: 数字系统带来了一类新的损失：预防便宜、承受昂贵，同一标签于是延伸到这一领域。

senses.title: Managing personal health risk
senses.definition: the everyday use of the same logic on one's own body, money and habits
senses.definitionCN: 把同样的逻辑用在自身身体、金钱与习惯上的日常说法
senses.example: Her doctor called her diet and exercise plan a form of risk management.
senses.exampleCN: 她的医生把她那份饮食与运动计划称作一种风险管理。
senses.why: the phrase moved from offices into clinics and homes because individuals also weigh a small present cost against a large future loss.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语从办公室走进诊所与家庭，因为个人同样会用眼前的小成本换取未来的大损失。

senses.title: Disaster and climate risk reduction
senses.titleCN: 灾害与气候风险的降低
senses.definition: public planning that lowers the damage expected from floods, heat and other natural shocks
senses.definitionCN: 为降低洪水、高温等自然冲击所造成损害而做的公共规划
senses.example: Coastal cities now treat flood risk management as a budget priority.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海城市如今把洪水风险管理列为预算优先项。
senses.why: public bodies borrowed the corporate term for the same arithmetic of likelihood and damage, applied to whole populations.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构借用了企业术语，因为其背后是同一套「可能性乘以损害」的算法，只是对象换成全体居民。

intro.en: The phrase joins risk, a word of uncertain Italian origin that reached English through French, with management, which descends from Latin manus 'hand' by way of an Italian verb for handling horses. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由 risk 与 management 合成：前者源自意大利语、来源不确定，经法语进入英语；后者经意大利语中「驯马、操控」的动词上溯到拉丁语 manus「手」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Risk first appears in Italian trading records as risco or rischio, meaning a hazard run in shipping. Its deeper origin is uncertain: a link to a Latin verb for cutting away, and a link to a Greek word for root or cliff, are both hypotheses, and neither is settled.
items.cn: 风险一词最早见于意大利商业记录，写作 risco 或 rischio，指航运中要冒的危险。其更深来源不确定：把它连到拉丁语「切去」的动词，或连到希腊语「根、崖」的词，都只是假说，均无定论。

items.en: French took the Italian word as risque, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century. The early English sense was the chance of loss in trade or at sea, not yet a formal discipline.
items.cn: 法语把这个意大利词吸收为 risque，英语于 16 世纪借用。早期英语义为贸易或海上的损失可能，还不是一门正式学问。

items.en: By the seventeenth century risk was used for any uncertain harm that could be priced, insured or shared, which prepared the ground for the later compound.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，风险已用于任何可以被定价、投保或分担的不确定损害，为此后的复合词铺路。

items.en: Manage came from Italian maneggiare 'to handle, to train a horse', built on mano 'hand', from Latin manus. The horse sense gives the word its feel of skilled, repeated control.
items.cn: 管理一词来自意大利语 maneggiare「操控、驯马」，基于 mano「手」，再上溯拉丁语 manus。驯马的义感让这个词带上「熟练而反复的控制」意味。

items.en: The noun management first named the act of handling something, then the group of people who conduct an enterprise, a shift recorded in business writing of the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 名词管理先指操控某物的动作，后指经营企业的一群人，这一转变见于 19 世纪的商业写作。

items.en: The full phrase took hold in the mid-twentieth century, when engineering, insurance and finance began to treat the control of risk as a measurable professional routine.
items.cn: 整个短语在 20 世纪中叶站住脚，当时工程、保险与金融开始把风险控制当作可计量的职业常规。

note.en: The first group holds look-alike words built on risk or on the handling root; the second holds near neighbours that name narrower or adjacent practices.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「风险」或「操控」词干、形近的词；第二组是范围更窄或相邻的近似说法。

entries.definition: Carrying danger; it describes the exposure itself, while risk management describes what is done about it.
entries.definitionCN: 指带有危险；它描述敞口本身，而风险管理描述针对敞口做了什么。

entries.definition: Claimed to carry no danger; the phrase is a goal, not the process that pursues it.
entries.definitionCN: 声称没有危险；这是一个目标，而不是追求它的过程。

entries.definition: To handle or control something with skill; management is its noun, and the compound adds what is being handled.
entries.definitionCN: 指以技巧操控；管理是其名词形式，复合词则补出所操控的对象。

entries.definition: To handle something badly; the prefix marks failure, the reverse of what the discipline aims at.
entries.definitionCN: 指处理得很糟；前缀标记失败，与该学问的目标相反。

entries.definition: The act of making a loss smaller; it is one stage inside risk management, not the whole cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 指使损失变小；它只是风险管理内部的一个环节，不是整个循环。

entries.definition: A contract that pays for a loss after it happens; it transfers risk rather than removing its cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指损失发生后予以赔付的合同；它转移风险，而非消除成因。

entries.definition: Work that prevents injury to people, usually in one workplace; risk management also weighs money and reputation.
entries.definitionCN: 指防止人身伤害的工作，通常限于一个场所；风险管理还要权衡金钱与声誉。

entries.definition: Taking an offsetting position so that a price move hurts less; it is one technique within the wider process.
entries.definitionCN: 指建立对冲头寸以减轻价格波动伤害；它是整个流程中的一种技术。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Risk is the uncertain harm; management is the skilled handling: the phrase reads as handling harm before it lands.
normal.cn: 风险是不确定的损害，管理是熟练的处理：整个短语读作「在损害落地前处理它」。

normal.en: The word family runs risk, risky, risk-free, risk manager, manage, management, managerial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括风险、有风险的、无风险的、风险经理、管理、管理层、管理上的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the level: enterprise, financial, project and operational risk management.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出层级：企业、金融、项目与运营风险管理。

normal.en: Manage came from horse training, so the image is a rider keeping an animal on course, not a clerk filing papers.
normal.cn: 管理一词来自驯马，所以意象是骑手让牲畜走在正路上，而不是文员整理文件。

normal.en: Insurance is the oldest branch: pay a small certain sum to avoid a large uncertain one.
normal.cn: 保险是最古老的分支：付出一笔确定的小钱，躲开一笔不确定的大钱。

abstract.en: Picture a weather map where every red patch already has a name beside it and a person assigned to it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张气象图，每块红色区域旁边都已写好名字，并指定了负责人。

abstract.en: Picture a ship's captain who sails anyway, but only after counting the lifeboats.
abstract.cn: 想象一位船长照旧出海，只是在数清救生艇之后才起锚。

abstract.en: Picture a household that keeps one drawer of candles and water, and never needs to think about it again.
abstract.cn: 想象一户人家在抽屉里备好蜡烛与清水，此后就不必再为此担心。

examples.en: Good risk management does not remove uncertainty; it makes the cost of being wrong bearable.
examples.cn: 好的风险管理并不消除不确定性，而是让判断出错的代价变得可以承受。

examples.en: The bank's risk management blocked the trade because it exceeded the single-name limit.
examples.cn: 银行的风险管理部门否决了这笔交易，因为它超过了单一对手方的限额。

examples.en: Flood risk management saved the district more than the new drainage system cost.
examples.cn: 洪水风险管理为该区挽回的损失超过了新排水系统的造价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「风险」加「管理」——先把可能出事的环节找出来，再安排人去管住它 → 风险管理

root: risk 源自意大利语 risco／rischio「航运中的危险」，经法语 risque 进入英语，更深来源不确定（有「切去」与「根、崖」两种假说）；management 经意大利语 maneggiare「操控、驯马」上溯拉丁语 manus「手」，加名词后缀而成。整个短语在 20 世纪中叶成为专业术语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one cycle: find the exposure, measure it, decide who carries it, and keep watching it. The cycle is then applied to money, to a whole firm, to a project, to an insurer, to a network, to a body and to a city.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个循环展开：先找出敞口，再衡量它，决定由谁承担，然后持续观察。这个循环再被用到金钱、整个企业、单个项目、保险公司、网络、个人身体与一座城市上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chart of every weak point, each with a colour, a name and a countermeasure beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张列满薄弱环节的图表，每一处都配有颜色、负责人与应对办法。

branches.en: PROCESS AND OFFICE: the same cycle is both a method and the team that runs it.
branches.cn: 流程与部门：同一个循环既是一套方法，也是执行它的团队。

branches.en: MONEY AND THE WHOLE FIRM: exposures are priced in markets, then balanced across every department at once.
branches.cn: 金钱与整个企业：敞口先在市场中被定价，再在各部门之间整体平衡。

branches.en: SHORT HORIZON AND TRANSFER: a project runs the cycle to a deadline, and insurance moves the loss to another party.
branches.cn: 短周期与转移：项目把循环跑到截止日，保险则把损失移给另一方。

branches.en: DIGITAL SURFACE: data and networks add a cheap-to-prevent, costly-to-suffer class of loss.
branches.cn: 数字表面：数据与网络添上一类「预防便宜、承受昂贵」的损失。

branches.en: BODY AND CITY: the same arithmetic is used on one person's habits and on a whole coastline.
branches.cn: 身体与城市：同一套算法被用在个人习惯上，也被用在整条海岸线上。

intro.en: The phrase is a native compound of two borrowed words. The risk half is of uncertain Romance origin; the manage half carries a Latin root for hand plus an Italian verb for handling.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个借词构成的原生复合词。前半「风险」的罗曼语来源不确定；后半「管理」带拉丁语「手」的词根与意大利语「操控」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Only the manage half has a clear Latin ancestor: manus 'hand' anchors the family that runs manage, manager, managerial and management.
latinIntro.cn: 只有「管理」这一半有清楚的拉丁语祖先：manus「手」支撑起管理、经理、管理上的与管理层这一族词。

items.example: The lender priced the risk into the interest rate.
items.exampleCN: 放贷方把这一风险计入利率。

items.example: The shortcut is risky in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这条捷径在冬天很危险。
没有投资是真正无风险的。

items.meaning: the person who runs the process
items.example: The risk manager chairs the weekly review.
items.exampleCN: 风险经理主持每周复核。

items.example: The manager approved the new schedule.

items.meaning: the act or body of managing
items.exampleCN: 管理层削减了差旅预算。

items.example: The workload is manageable this month.
items.exampleCN: 这个月的工作量还应付得来。

items.example: The fund was mismanaged for years.
items.exampleCN: 这只基金多年来管理失当。

definition_zh: adj. 重要的，重大的；作为结果的，随之而来的
definition_en: important, or happening as a result
core_image: 一枚棋子落下，整盘局势随之改观
scene: 这是一项重大决定，会影响许多人的一生。 This is a consequential decision that will shape many lives.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：consequential 指重大的；句意是这项决定会影响许多人的一生。

pos.zh: 重大的；作为结果的

senses.title: Carrying weight
senses.definition: important enough to change things
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以改变局面
senses.example: This is a consequential decision.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一项重大决定。
senses.why: The word weighs outcomes, not just facts.
senses.whyCN: 该词衡量的是后果的重量。

senses.title: Following as an effect
senses.titleCN: 作为结果的，随之而来的
senses.definition: arising as a result of something else
senses.definitionCN: 由另一事引起
senses.example: The consequential costs were high.
senses.exampleCN: 随之而来的费用很高。
senses.why: Latin consequi means to follow after.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 consequi 意为随后跟随。

intro.en: Consequential extends consequent with a Latin adjective ending.
intro.cn: consequential 给 consequent 加上了拉丁形容词词尾。

items.en: Sequi means to follow.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随。

items.en: Consequi means to follow after.
items.cn: consequi 意为随后跟随。

items.en: Consequentia names what follows.
items.cn: consequentia 指跟随而来之物。

items.en: English used it of logical results.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语用它指逻辑结果。

items.en: It came to mean weighty in effect.
items.cn: 十九世纪引申为「影响重大」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the consequ- stem; the near-meaning group names weight and result.
note.cn: 形近组共享 consequ- 词干；近义组列出分量与结果。

entries.definition: An effect of an action.
entries.definitionCN: 行为的结果。

entries.definition: Following as a result.
entries.definitionCN: 随之发生的。

entries.definition: As a result.
entries.definitionCN: 因此。

entries.definition: Mattering a great deal.
entries.definitionCN: 非常重要的。

entries.definition: Large enough to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 重要到值得注意的。

entries.definition: Very important in effect.
entries.definitionCN: 影响深远的。

entries.definition: Produced by a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 由原因产生的。

normalIntro.en: A consequential thing either follows from much or decides much.
normalIntro.cn: consequential 之物或因前因而来，或因分量而重。

normal.en: Consequent means following.
normal.cn: consequent 意为跟随。

normal.en: -ial widens it into an adjective of weight.
normal.cn: -ial 把它扩展为表分量的形容词。

normal.en: A consequential choice changes lives.
normal.cn: 重大选择改变人生。

normal.en: Consequential loss follows another loss.
normal.cn: 间接损失随另一损失而来。

normal.en: The two senses meet at consequence.
normal.cn: 两义都汇于 consequence。

abstract.en: One chess piece moved, the board changed.
abstract.cn: 一枚棋子落下，棋盘改观。

abstract.en: A stone dropped into still water.
abstract.cn: 投入静水的一颗石子。

abstract.en: A signature that moves a nation.
abstract.cn: 推动一个国家的一笔签名。

examples.en: The court called it a consequential error.
examples.cn: 法院称这是影响重大的错误。

examples.en: Consequential damage is covered by the policy.
examples.cn: 间接损害在保单范围内。

examples.en: Her work proved consequential for the field.
examples.cn: 她的工作对该领域影响深远。

dict_mnemonic.text: consequent（跟随的）+ -ial（…的）→ 随之而来的；引申为分量重大的。

root: 拉丁 consequi（随后跟随）→ consequentia（后果）→ 英语 consequential

sensesIntro.en: What follows from a cause, and what is heavy enough to matter.
sensesIntro.cn: 由原因而来的东西，以及重到不可忽视的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one piece moved and the whole board changed
core.cn: 核心意象：落下一子，全盘改观

branches.en: A vote that decides a war.
branches.cn: 决定战争走向的一票。

branches.en: A voice that carries in the room.
branches.cn: 在屋里举足轻重的声音。

branches.en: A cost that follows a delay.
branches.cn: 随延误而来的费用。

branches.en: A loss caused by a closure.
branches.cn: 因停业造成的损失。

branches.en: Heavy because it follows far.
branches.cn: 因其影响深远而沉重。

intro.en: Consequential is the weighty cousin of consequent.

definition_zh: n. 复制；重复；副本；（生物）重复段
definition_en: the act of making an exact copy, a needless repeat of work, or a thing produced as a second copy
core_image: 复印机连续吐出同一页纸，纸盘里叠成一模一样的一摞；同一间办公室两面墙上贴着同一张进度表，各由一个队伍更新；档案柜里正本与副本并放，副本角上盖着「复制」章

sceneCN: 这里 duplication 指「制作与某物完全一样的副本这一行为」（第 1 个义项：复制）；句意是复制这份文件只花了一分钟。图中可辨识物件：复印机、一模一样的一摞纸、对齐的订书钉孔。

senses.title: Making a copy
senses.definition: the act of making an exact copy of something
senses.definitionCN: （名词）制作与某物完全一样的副本这一行为
senses.example: The duplication of the file took only a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 复制这份文件只花了一分钟。
senses.why: A copier keeps handing out the same page until the tray holds one identical stack.
senses.whyCN: 复印机不停吐出同一页，直到纸盘里叠成一模一样的一摞。

senses.title: A needless repeat
senses.definition: the act of doing something again so that effort or material is wasted
senses.definitionCN: （名词）把某事再做一遍，致使人手或材料白费
senses.example: Two departments ran the same survey, a duplication of effort nobody had planned.

senses.title: A second copy

senses.definitionCN: （名词）作为另一物的完全复制品而产生的东西
senses.example: The archive keeps a duplication of every signed contract in a separate room.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆在另一个房间保存着每份已签合同的副本。
senses.why: A cabinet holds the original and its copy, the copy stamped in one corner.
senses.whyCN: 档案柜里放着正本与副本，副本角上盖着一个章。

intro.en: Duplication is the noun of duplicare, to fold twice: the ending -ation turns the folding into an act, so duplication is either the making of a second copy or the copy that results.
intro.cn: duplication 是 duplicare「折两次」的名词：-ation 把折叠变成一个行为，所以 duplication 既指做出第二份的动作，也指由此产生的那一份。

dict_mnemonic.text: duplication ＝ duplicate（复制）＋ -ation（行为名词后缀）＝「折成两份这件事」。拉丁语 duo（二）＋ plicare（折叠）→ duplicare「折两次」。三个用法要分清：duplication of the file 是「复制文件」（有用），duplication of effort 是「重复劳动」（白费），gene duplication 是「基因重复」（演化的原料）。avoid duplication 是公文里最常见的「避免重复」。别和 duplicity（两面派）混。

definition_zh: 神经元；神经细胞
definition_en: a cell of the nervous system that receives signals and passes them on to other nerve cells
core_image: 一个带许多触须的小节点，一头接上线，另一头把信号递出去
scene: 显微镜下，一张神经组织的图里，一个细长的节点伸出许多分支，连向四周： Each neuron sends its signal along a single long fibre.
sceneCN: 这里指「神经元」这一细胞单位（第 1 个义项：神经系统中传递信号的细胞）；句意为每个神经元沿一条长纤维把信号送出。

pos.zh: 神经元；神经细胞（神经系统的基本单元）
（人工神经网络中的）神经元单元

derivatives.zh: 神经毡（神经纤维与胶质构成的网）

senses.title: The nerve cell
senses.titleCN: 神经元：神经系统的基本细胞单位
senses.definition: a cell with a body, one or more long fibres and many branches, which receives and transmits nerve signals
senses.definitionCN: 具有胞体、一条或多条长纤维与许多分支、能接收并传导神经信号的细胞
senses.example: Each neuron sends its signal along a single long fibre.
senses.exampleCN: 每个神经元沿一条长纤维把信号送出。
senses.why: The cell is defined by its shape as much as its tissue: a compact body with a long output line is what makes point-to-point signalling possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个细胞既由组织定义，也由形状定义：紧凑的胞体加一条长输出线，才使点对点传导成为可能。

senses.title: Sensory neuron
senses.titleCN: 感觉神经元：把外界信息送进来
senses.definition: a neuron that carries signals from a sense organ or receptor toward the central nervous system
senses.definitionCN: 把来自感觉器官或感受器的信号传向中枢神经系统的神经元
senses.example: A sensory neuron reports the heat of the cup to the spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉神经元把杯子的热度报告给脊髓。
senses.why: Direction defines this type: the signal travels inward, so the cell is named for the side it serves.
senses.whyCN: 方向定义了这一类型：信号向内走，因此这个细胞按它所服务的一端命名。

senses.title: Motor neuron
senses.titleCN: 运动神经元：把指令送出去
senses.definition: a neuron that carries signals from the central nervous system to a muscle or gland
senses.definitionCN: 把信号从中枢神经系统传到肌肉或腺体的神经元
senses.example: A motor neuron tells the hand to close around the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 运动神经元让手合拢握住杯子。
senses.why: This is the mirror image of the sensory type: the same cell structure, with the signal pointed outward.
senses.whyCN: 这是感觉型的镜像：同样的细胞结构，信号朝外指。

senses.title: Interneuron
senses.titleCN: 中间神经元：在系统内部转接
senses.definition: a neuron that connects other neurons inside the central nervous system rather than reaching the body's surface
senses.definitionCN: 在中枢神经系统内部连接其他神经元、不直接到达体表的神经元
senses.example: An interneuron passes the signal from a sensory cell to a motor cell.
senses.exampleCN: 中间神经元把信号从感觉细胞传给运动细胞。
senses.why: Most neurons neither enter nor leave the body; they sit between, which is why the name simply marks the middle position.
senses.whyCN: 大多数神经元既不进入也不离开身体，而是位于中间，因此名称只标记中间位置。

senses.title: Artificial neuron
senses.titleCN: 人工神经元：计算模型中的单元
senses.definition: a simple computing unit that takes several inputs, weights them and passes one output on
senses.definitionCN: 接收若干输入、加权后输出一个信号的简单计算单元
senses.example: Each artificial neuron adds its inputs and fires above a threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人工神经元把输入相加，超过阈值就「放电」。
senses.why: The machine keeps only the input-weight-output shape of the cell, which is why the biological name was borrowed.
senses.whyCN: 机器只保留细胞「输入—加权—输出」的形状，因此借用了生物学名称。

senses.title: Anatomy of a neuron
senses.titleCN: 神经元的解剖形态（胞体、轴突、树突）
senses.definition: the parts of a nerve cell: cell body, axon and dendrites, each with a different role in signalling
senses.definitionCN: 神经细胞的组成部分：胞体、轴突与树突，各自在传导中承担不同角色
senses.example: The axon of a neuron can be longer than the whole spinal cord segment.
senses.exampleCN: 一个神经元的轴突可能比整段脊髓还长。
senses.why: Once the cell is understood as a device, its parts are named by the direction in which they pass the signal.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把细胞理解为装置，它的各部分就按传导方向命名。

senses.title: Neuron degeneration
senses.definition: the loss or wasting of nerve cells, as in several progressive diseases
senses.definitionCN: 神经细胞的丧失或萎缩，见于若干进行性疾病
senses.example: The disease slowly destroys the neurons that control walking.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病逐渐破坏控制行走的神经元。
senses.why: When cells are lost they are not replaced easily, so clinical talk focuses on the unit rather than the whole system.
senses.whyCN: 细胞丧失后不易补充，因此临床讨论聚焦于这一单位而非整个系统。

senses.title: The functional unit
senses.titleCN: 作为功能单元的神经元
senses.definition: the smallest unit that can receive, integrate and pass on a nerve signal
senses.definitionCN: 能接收、整合并传出神经信号的最小单位
senses.example: Physiologists treat the neuron as the functional unit of the nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 生理学家把神经元视为神经系统的功能单位。
senses.why: A unit is defined by what it can do alone, and a single cell can take in, sum and send a signal.
senses.whyCN: 单位由它能独立完成的事定义，而单个细胞就能接收、汇总并发出信号。

intro.en: Neuron is Greek neuron, meaning sinew, cord or nerve. The modern sense of a nerve cell dates from nineteenth-century microscopy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: neuron 即希腊语 neuron，意为筋、索或神经。指神经细胞的现代义来自 19 世纪显微解剖学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek neuron meant sinew, cord or nerve, and it could name both the string-like structure and the bodily organ of feeling.
items.cn: 希腊 neuron 意为筋、索或神经，既可指索状结构，也可指身体的感觉器官。

items.en: Latin nervus is the cognate of neuron and supplies the rival English family nerve and nervous; the shared ancestor is reconstructed.
items.cn: 拉丁 nervus 与 neuron 同源，提供英语的另一支 nerve 与 nervous；共同祖形为重构形式。

items.en: Early anatomists used neuron for the nerve fibre or the whole cord, not yet for a single cell.
items.cn: 早期解剖学家用 neuron 指神经纤维或整条索，尚未指单个细胞。

items.en: Improved microscopes and staining showed that nerve tissue is made of discrete cells, and the cell sense of neuron took hold.
items.cn: 显微镜与染色的进步显示神经组织由离散的细胞构成，neuron 的细胞义由此确立。

items.en: The cell sense is usually credited to late nineteenth-century work, including the naming associated with Wilhelm Waldeyer in 1891; the exact first use is debated.
items.cn: 细胞义通常归功于 19 世纪后期的工作，包括 1891 年与 Wilhelm Waldeyer 相关的命名；确切的最早使用仍有争议。

items.en: Twentieth-century neuroscience added the artificial neuron and the neuron doctrine, extending the word beyond anatomy.
items.cn: 20 世纪神经科学又添人工神经元与神经元学说，把这个词扩展到解剖学之外。

note.en: The first group holds look-alike words and spelling variants; the second holds the parts and neighbours of a neuron.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词与拼写变体；第二组是神经元的部件与邻近结构。

entries.definition: A particle with no charge in an atomic nucleus; it is one letter away in sound but belongs to physics, not biology.
entries.definitionCN: 原子核中不带电的粒子；读音只差一点，却属于物理而非生物。

entries.definition: A British variant spelling of neuron; it is the same cell, not a different structure.
entries.definitionCN: neuron 的英式变体拼写；指同一个细胞，不是另一种结构。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves or nerve cells; it describes, while neuron names the cell.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经或神经细胞有关的；它作描述，neuron 命名细胞。

entries.definition: The tangled mass of fibres and glia between nerve cell bodies; it is tissue, not a single cell.
entries.definitionCN: 神经细胞体之间纤维与胶质缠结的团块；它是组织，不是单个细胞。

entries.definition: The everyday term for a neuron; it says what the cell is without using the Greek word.
entries.definitionCN: 神经元的日常说法；不用希腊词而直接说明这个细胞是什么。

entries.definition: The long fibre that carries a signal away from the cell body; it is a part of a neuron.
entries.definitionCN: 把信号从胞体带走的长纤维；它是神经元的一部分。

entries.definition: A branching fibre that receives signals and brings them toward the cell body.
entries.definitionCN: 接收信号并把信号带向胞体的分支纤维。

entries.definition: The gap or junction where one neuron passes a signal to another; it belongs to neither cell alone.
entries.definitionCN: 一个神经元把信号传给另一个的间隙或接头；它不属于任一细胞单独所有。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek cord word, the real cell doctrine and the real parts of the cell.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊索状词、真实的细胞学说与真实的细胞部件。

normal.en: Greek neuron meant cord, and a nerve cell is a tiny cord with branches.
normal.cn: 希腊 neuron 意为索，而神经细胞就是一根带分支的微小索。

normal.en: The three functional types are named by direction: sensory in, motor out, interneuron between.
normal.cn: 三种功能类型按方向命名：感觉向内、运动向外、中间神经元居中。

normal.en: Axon carries away, dendrite brings in, and the cell body sits between them.
normal.cn: 轴突带出，树突带入，胞体位于两者之间。

normal.en: An artificial neuron keeps only the shape: inputs, weights, one output.
normal.cn: 人工神经元只保留形状：输入、权重、一个输出。

normal.en: In British spelling the word can also be written neurone, with the same meaning.
normal.cn: 英式拼写也可写作 neurone，意思完全相同。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny switchboard with many incoming wires and one outgoing wire.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小交换机，许多线进来，一根线出去。

abstract.en: Picture a relay runner who receives a baton and passes it on without keeping it.
abstract.cn: 想象接力跑者，接到棒就传下去，从不把棒留在手里。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd where each person can only whisper to a neighbour, yet a message crosses the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人只能对邻座耳语，消息却能传遍整个房间。

examples.en: A single neuron can connect to thousands of others.
examples.cn: 一个神经元可以连接数千个其他神经元。

examples.en: Motor neurons weaken in the disease that gradually removes movement.
examples.cn: 在那种逐渐夺走运动能力的疾病中，运动神经元会变弱。

examples.en: The model treats each neuron as a simple weighted sum.
examples.cn: 该模型把每个神经元当作一个简单的加权求和。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛龙」（neuron）——一头牛身上布满细索，每个结都是一个细胞 → 神经元

root: 希腊 neuron「筋、索、神经」，与拉丁 nervus 同源；指单个神经细胞的现代义形成于 19 世纪显微解剖学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one cell: the basic unit, three directional types, the artificial unit, its anatomy, its degeneration, and finally its status as the functional unit of the system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述同一个细胞：基本单位、三种方向类型、人工单元、解剖形态、退化损伤，最后是它作为系统功能单位的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small node with many feelers in and one long line out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小节点，许多触须伸进来，一条长线伸出去。

branches.en: THE CELL AND ITS PARTS: the unit as a whole, and the body, axon and dendrites that make it.
branches.cn: 细胞与部件：作为整体的单位，以及构成它的胞体、轴突与树突。

branches.en: THREE DIRECTIONS: inward, outward and between.
branches.cn: 三个方向：向内、向外与居中。

branches.en: THE MACHINE COPY: inputs, weights and one output.
branches.cn: 机器复制品：输入、权重与一个输出。

branches.en: WHEN CELLS DIE: loss of the unit removes the function.
branches.cn: 细胞死亡时：单位的丧失带走功能。

branches.en: WHY IT COUNTS AS A UNIT: it can receive, sum and send on its own.
branches.cn: 为何算作单位：它能独立完成接收、汇总与发出。

intro.en: Neuron is a Greek noun; its English family grows through the suffixes -al, -al + -ly and compounds such as neuropil.

latinIntro.en: Greek neuron entered Latin medical writing and shares a root with Latin nervus; the adjective neuronalis is a modern scientific formation.

items.example: Neuropil fills the spaces between neurons.
