definition_zh: 股票市场；股票交易所；股市行情
definition_en: the market in which shares of companies are bought and sold
core_image: 一座喧闹的拍卖大厅，无数公司股份在报价声中易手
scene: 午后的交易大厅里，大屏幕上的指数快速下滑，经纪人纷纷抛售手中股份。 The stock market fell sharply after the central bank raised interest rates.
sceneCN: 这里指「股票市场整体」，对应第 1 个义项：买卖公司股份的市场；句意为央行加息后股市大幅下跌。画面要点：交易大厅、行情大屏、下单电话。

pos.zh: 股票市场；股市（可指交易场所、交易体系或整体行情）

senses.title: The market where shares are traded
senses.definition: the system or place in which shares of public companies are bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 公开买卖公司股份的体系或场所
senses.example: Pension funds are major players in the stock market.
senses.exampleCN: 养老基金是股票市场的重要参与者。
senses.why: Stock supplies the object and market supplies the meeting place for exchange, so the compound names the arena where shares change hands.
senses.whyCN: stock 提供交易对象，market 提供交换的场所，复合词因此指股份易手的场域。

senses.title: The secondary market for listed shares
senses.titleCN: 已上市股份的二级交易市场
senses.definition: the market in which existing shares are traded after the company has listed them
senses.definitionCN: 公司上市之后，已有股份在投资者之间转手的市场
senses.example: Most trading on the stock market happens between investors, not with the company.
senses.exampleCN: 股票市场上的交易大多发生在投资者之间，而不是与公司本身进行。
senses.why: Once shares exist, the market lets owners exchange them without the company issuing anything new, so the arena becomes a second-hand market for claims.
senses.whyCN: 股份一旦存在，市场就让持有者在彼此之间交换，公司不再发行新东西，于是这个场域成了权利主张的二手市场。

senses.title: The level of prices at a time
senses.definition: the general level or direction of share prices at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻股份价格的总体水平或走向
senses.example: The stock market was up three percent by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 到中午时股市上涨了三个百分点。
senses.why: Because the arena is visible mainly through its prices, the name shifts from the place to the number that the place produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个场域主要通过价格显现，于是名称从场所转到场所产生的数字上。

senses.title: The physical exchange building
senses.definition: the building or floor where dealers meet to trade shares
senses.definitionCN: 交易员聚集买卖股份的建筑或交易大厅
senses.example: Tourists photographed the old stock market on Wall Street.
senses.exampleCN: 游客在华尔街拍摄那座古老的证券交易所。
senses.why: Before screens, the market was a room full of shouted orders, so the compound keeps a literal architectural sense.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕时代之前，市场就是一间充满喊价的屋子，因此这个复合词仍保留字面的建筑义。

senses.title: A barometer of the economy
senses.titleCN: 作为经济晴雨表的股市
senses.definition: the stock market understood as an indicator of economic confidence
senses.definitionCN: 被当作经济信心指标的股票市场
senses.example: Policymakers watch the stock market for signs of panic.
senses.exampleCN: 政策制定者观察股市以寻找恐慌迹象。
senses.why: Prices aggregate many people's expectations, so the arena is read as a signal about the wider economy rather than only about companies.
senses.whyCN: 价格汇总了许多人的预期，于是这个场域被读成关于更广经济的信号，而不只是关于公司。

senses.title: The global network of exchanges
senses.titleCN: 全球各交易所组成的网络
senses.definition: the worldwide system of linked exchanges trading shares around the clock
senses.definitionCN: 全球各地交易所在不同时区连成的股份交易体系
senses.example: A shock in one stock market spreads to others within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个股市的震荡会在数小时内传到其他股市。
senses.why: When many local arenas are connected by information and capital flows, the singular name stands for the whole network.
senses.whyCN: 当许多地方场域被信息与资本流动连在一起，单数的名称就代表整个网络。

senses.title: A speculative arena
senses.definition: the stock market seen as a place of speculation, euphoria and sudden loss
senses.definitionCN: 被视为投机、狂热与骤然亏损之所的股市
senses.example: He lost his savings in the stock market.
senses.exampleCN: 他在股市里赔掉了积蓄。
senses.why: The arena language invites a figurative reading in which traders are players and prices are bets, so the word can name a gamble.
senses.whyCN: 「场域」的说法引出比喻读法：交易者是玩家，价格是赌注，于是这个词也能指一场赌博。

senses.title: Public judgement of company value
senses.titleCN: 对公司价值的公开评判
senses.definition: the daily public assessment of what companies are worth
senses.definitionCN: 每天由市场给出的公司价值评估
senses.example: The stock market valued the startup at twice its sales.
senses.exampleCN: 股市给这家初创公司的估值达到其销售额的两倍。
senses.why: Each trade is a small verdict on value, so the arena becomes a continuous public judgement rather than a mere meeting place.
senses.whyCN: 每一笔交易都是对价值的一次小裁决，于是这个场域成了持续的公开评判，而不只是会面之处。

intro.en: Stock market joins two words of different origins: a Germanic stock for the shares and a Latin market for the place of trade. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stock market 把两个来源不同的词拼在一起：表示股份的日耳曼语 stock，与表示交易场所的拉丁语 market。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stock first meant a post or trunk and later a stored fund; in finance it came to mean the capital of a company divided into shares.
items.cn: stock 最初指木桩或树干，后来指储存的资金；在金融中转而指被分成股份的公司资本。

items.en: Mercatus meant trade or a marketplace, from mercari 'to trade' and merx 'merchandise', the source of merchant and mercantile.
items.cn: mercatus 意为交易或集市，出自 mercari「做买卖」与 merx「商品」，也是 merchant 与 mercantile 的来源。

items.en: Market entered English through Old North French and settled as the ordinary word for a place where buyers and sellers meet.
items.cn: market 经古北法语进入英语，逐渐固定为买卖双方会面之处的常用词。

items.en: The compound stock market is generally dated to the early nineteenth century, when organized exchanges and daily share lists became common.
items.cn: 复合词 stock market 一般定在十九世纪早期，当时有组织的交易所与每日股价表开始普及。

items.en: Electronic trading detached the market from any single floor and made the singular name stand for a worldwide network.
items.cn: 电子交易把市场与任何单一交易大厅分开，使单数名称代表一个全球网络。

note.en: The first group contains phrases that look nearly identical but point to the exchange or the place rather than the market as a whole; the second group names the same arena from other vocabularies.
note.cn: 第一组是看起来几乎相同、却指交易所或场所而非整体市场的说法；第二组用别的词汇指同一场域。

entries.definition: The organized institution that runs trading in shares; it is the venue and operator, while the stock market is the wider activity and price level.
entries.definitionCN: 组织股份交易的有形机构；它指场所与运营者，而股票市场指更广的交易活动与价格水平。

entries.definition: Any place, physical or digital, where buyers and sellers meet; it lacks the specific link to company shares.
entries.definitionCN: 任何实体或数字的买卖双方会面之处；不含与公司股份的具体联系。

entries.definition: The shares themselves; the market is the arena, while stock is what is traded inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 股份本身；market 是场域，stock 是场域中被交易的东西。

entries.definition: A general system of exchange; alone it can mean any trade in goods, services or labour.
entries.definitionCN: 一般的交换体系；单独使用时可以指任何商品、服务或劳动力的交易。

entries.definition: The market for equity, meaning shares; it is the formal finance term for the same arena.
entries.definitionCN: 权益即股份的市场；这是同一场域的正式金融说法。

entries.definition: A common synonym in Australian and New Zealand usage, built on share instead of stock.
entries.definitionCN: 澳大利亚与新西兰常用的同义说法，用 share 而不是 stock 构成。

entries.definition: A continental European stock exchange, especially in French-speaking countries; it names an institution rather than the abstract market.
entries.definitionCN: 欧洲大陆的证券交易所，尤指法语地区；它指机构而非抽象市场。

entries.definition: The market for long-term funds, including both shares and bonds; the stock market is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 长期资金市场，包括股票与债券；股票市场只是其中一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves of the compound, real synonyms and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词两个真实的组成部分、真实同义词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Stock is what is traded; market is where it is traded, so the phrase is transparent.
normal.cn: stock 是被交易的东西，market 是交易发生的地方，所以这个短语一目了然。

normal.en: Stock itself began as a post or trunk and later became stored capital, which is why shares are called stock.
normal.cn: stock 本指木桩或树干，后来变成储存的资本，股份因此被称为 stock。

normal.en: Market comes from a Latin word for trade, the same source as merchant and mercantile.
normal.cn: market 出自拉丁语表示交易词，与 merchant、mercantile 同源。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show its force: crash, rally, index, bubble.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示它的力度：崩盘、反弹、指数、泡沫。

normal.en: Stock exchange is the institution; stock market is the activity and the price level.
normal.cn: 证券交易所是机构，股票市场是活动与价格水平。

abstract.en: Picture a vast room where every shout is a tiny verdict on what a company is worth.
abstract.cn: 想象一间巨大的厅堂，每一声喊价都是对公司价值的一次微小裁决。

abstract.en: Picture prices as weather over that room, rising and falling while the floor stays fixed.
abstract.cn: 把价格想成那间厅堂上空的天气，起伏变化而地面不动。

abstract.en: Picture the room dissolving into screens, so the place becomes a network without walls.
abstract.cn: 想象厅堂化入屏幕，场所于是变成没有围墙的网络。

examples.en: The stock market reacted calmly to the election result.
examples.cn: 股市对选举结果反应平静。

examples.en: Small investors can now enter the stock market through apps.
examples.cn: 小投资者现在可以通过应用程序进入股市。

examples.en: A falling stock market often precedes a slowdown in hiring.
examples.cn: 股市下跌往往先于招聘放缓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「stock（股份）+ market（市场）」——买卖股份的市场 → 股票市场

root: stock 出自古英语 stocc「木桩、树干」，后来指储存的资本与股份；market 出自拉丁语 mercatus「交易、集市」，经古北法语进入英语。两者在十九世纪初合成 stock market。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the arena itself to its prices, its buildings, its economic signal, its global network and finally to its speculative and judgemental force.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从场域本身出发，依次转到价格、建筑、经济信号、全球网络，最后落到投机与评判的力量上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowded trading floor where every shouted order is a small verdict on value.
core.cn: 核心意象：拥挤的交易大厅，每一次喊单都是对价值的一次小裁决。

branches.en: THE ARENA: the market is first the meeting place where listed shares change hands.
branches.cn: 场域：市场首先是已上市股份易手的会面之处。

branches.en: PRICE LEVEL: the place is then read through the number it produces each day.
branches.cn: 价格水平：场所再通过它每天产生的数字被读取。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: before screens, the arena was a literal room with a floor and a crowd.
branches.cn: 建筑：屏幕时代之前，场域就是一间有地面、有人群的真实屋子。

branches.en: SIGNAL AND NETWORK: many local arenas linked together become a barometer and a worldwide system.
branches.cn: 信号与网络：许多地方场域连在一起，成了晴雨表与全球体系。

branches.en: GAMBLE AND VERDICT: the same arena can be a place of speculation or a continuous public judgement of worth.
branches.cn: 博弈与裁决：同一场域既可以是投机之地，也可以是对价值的持续公开评判。

intro.en: Stock market combines a Germanic noun and a Latin-derived noun, and each half brings its own small family of compounds.
intro.cn: stock market 由一个日耳曼语名词与一个拉丁来源名词合成，两半各自带来一小族复合词。

latinIntro.en: Market descends from Latin mercatus, which also gives merchant, mercantile and commerce.
latinIntro.cn: market 源自拉丁语 mercatus，merchant、mercantile 与 commerce 也出自这一支。

items.meaning: a place or system of trade
several national or regional share markets
items.meaningCN: 多个国家或地区的股票市场

items.meaning: used before a noun to describe market-related things
items.meaningCN: 作定语，修饰与股市相关的事物
items.exampleCN: 股市规则去年发生了变化。

items.meaning: a place or platform of trade
items.example: The app became a marketplace for used cars.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用成了二手车交易平台。

items.meaning: a person who promotes or sells
items.exampleCN: 营销人员研究买家习惯。
这个设计被证明非常好卖。

latinEntries.meaning: a person who buys and sells goods
the exchange of goods on a large scale

definition_zh: 造林；植树成林；森林覆盖的建立
definition_en: the act or process of establishing forest cover by planting or sowing trees on land
core_image: 一片荒坡先被挖出整齐的树穴，随后苗木成片栽下，几年后连成绿色覆盖
scene: 荒坡上先挖出一排排树穴，随后苗木被成片栽下，几年后这里重新有了连续的林冠。 Rows of planting pits were dug on the bare slope, seedlings were set out in blocks, and within a few years continuous forest cover had returned: that whole effort is forestation.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「建立森林覆盖的整个努力」（第 1 个义项：通过栽植建立森林）；句意为荒坡先挖穴、再成片栽苗，几年后恢复连续林冠，这一整套工作就是造林。

pos.zh: 造林；植树成林
森林覆盖的建立过程
新造林（在原本无林的土地上）
重新造林（在曾经有林的土地上）
大规模植树计划
造林结果；已建立的林地
为碳汇或气候目的进行的造林
土地用途转为林地

senses.title: Establishing forest cover
senses.definition: the act or process of establishing a forest on land by planting or sowing trees
senses.definitionCN: 通过栽植或播种在土地上建立森林的行为或过程
senses.example: Forestation began with a survey of the eroded slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 造林从对侵蚀坡地的调查开始。
senses.why: This is the umbrella sense: any deliberate creation of forest cover.
senses.whyCN: 这是总称义：任何有意建立森林覆盖的行为。

senses.title: Process over time
senses.titleCN: 随时间推进的造林过程
senses.definition: the multi-year process by which planted land develops into functioning forest
senses.definitionCN: 栽植土地在多年中发育为功能森林的过程
senses.example: Forestation is measured in decades, not seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 造林以十年计，而不是以季节计。
senses.why: The word can name the slow process rather than the single planting event.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以命名缓慢过程，而不是一次栽植事件。

senses.title: Afforestation on bare land
senses.definition: the creation of forest on land that has not recently carried forest
senses.definitionCN: 在近期没有森林的土地上建立森林
senses.example: Afforestation converted the old pasture into a new wood.
senses.exampleCN: 新造林把旧牧场变成一片新林地。
senses.why: Technical usage separates new forest on bare land from replanting after loss.
senses.whyCN: 技术用法把裸地上的新林与损失后的补植区分开。

senses.title: Reforestation after loss
senses.titleCN: 森林损失后的重新造林
senses.definition: the replanting of land that was formerly forested but has lost its tree cover
senses.definitionCN: 在曾经有林、后来失去树冠的土地上重新栽植
senses.example: Reforestation followed the fire that burned the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊被火烧过之后进行了重新造林。
senses.why: The same act is named by its history: the land remembers a previous forest.
senses.whyCN: 同一动作按土地历史命名：这块地记得从前的森林。

senses.title: Large-scale planting program
senses.definition: an organized program that plants many hectares or millions of seedlings
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地栽植许多公顷或数百万株苗木的计划
senses.example: The national forestation program planted a billion trees.
senses.exampleCN: 国家造林计划栽下了十亿棵树。
senses.why: Scale turns a practice into a policy instrument with targets and budgets.
senses.whyCN: 规模把实践变成有目标与预算的政策工具。

senses.title: Resulting forest area
senses.definition: the forest area that results from planting, considered as an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 栽植所产生的森林面积，作为结果来看
senses.example: The forestation now covers the whole western slope.
senses.exampleCN: 新造的林地现在覆盖整个西坡。
senses.why: The action noun also names its product: the area that now carries forest.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词也命名产物：现在长着森林的那片面积。

senses.title: Carbon or climate forestation
senses.definition: forestation undertaken to absorb carbon or meet climate targets
senses.definitionCN: 为吸收碳或达成气候目标而进行的造林
senses.example: Carbon forestation is counted in tonnes of carbon dioxide stored.
senses.exampleCN: 碳汇造林以储存的二氧化碳吨数计量。
senses.why: The purpose changes the name: the forest is valued for stored carbon rather than timber.
senses.whyCN: 目的改变名称：这片森林的价值在储存的碳，而不在木材。

senses.title: Land-use conversion
senses.definition: the change of land use from agriculture or bare ground to forest
senses.definitionCN: 把农业用地或裸地改为林地
senses.example: Forestation changed the hydrology of the catchment within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 造林在十年内改变了这个集水区的水文状况。
senses.why: Seen from land-use planning, planting trees is a change of category, not only an act on a slope.
senses.whyCN: 从土地利用规划看，种树是类别改变，而不只是坡上的一项动作。

intro.en: Forestation is an English formation on forest plus the Latin-derived suffix -ation. Its technical branches, especially afforestation and reforestation, are nineteenth- and twentieth-century developments.
intro.cn: 该词由 forest 与拉丁来源后缀 -ation 构成；技术分支 afforestation、reforestation 在十九至二十世纪定型，具体年代为大致估计。

items.en: The base forest comes from Medieval Latin forestis through Old French. The suffix -ation comes from Latin -atio, which names an action or its result.
items.cn: 基础词 forest 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 forestis。后缀 -ation 来自拉丁语 -atio，命名动作或结果。

items.en: Forestation is recorded in nineteenth-century writing on land improvement. It was used alongside afforestation and reforestation, which became the more technical terms.
items.cn: forestation 见于十九世纪有关土地改良的写作。它与 afforestation、reforestation 并用，后两者后来成为更技术的术语。

items.en: Forestry separated afforestation, planting on land without recent forest, from reforestation, replanting after loss. Forestation remained the general cover term.
items.cn: 林业把 afforestation（在近期无林地上栽植）与 reforestation（损失后补植）分开；forestation 则保留为总称。

items.en: State tree-planting programs and soil-conservation schemes made forestation a policy word with targets, budgets and measured areas.
items.cn: 国家植树计划与水土保持方案使 forestation 成为带有目标、预算与测量面积的政策词。

items.en: Climate policy added carbon forestation, where the purpose is storage of carbon rather than timber or soil protection.
items.cn: 气候政策增加了碳汇造林，其目的不是木材或水土保护，而是碳储存。

note.en: The first group is close in sound or shares the base; the second group names the same act at different scales or from the opposite direction.
note.cn: 第一组读音接近或共享基础词；第二组在不同尺度或相反方向上命名同一行为。

entries.definition: the removal of forest cover; it is the reverse process, not a variant spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 毁林。除去森林覆盖，是相反过程，不是拼写变体。

entries.definition: planting a forest on land that has not recently been forested; it is a technical subtype of forestation.
entries.definitionCN: 新造林。在近期无林的土地上造林，是 forestation 的技术子类。

entries.definition: replanting land that was previously forested; it is another technical subtype.
entries.definitionCN: 重新造林。在曾经有林的土地上补植，是另一个技术子类。

entries.definition: the everyday act of planting trees; it does not require the result to become a forest.
entries.definitionCN: 植树。日常说法，不要求最终形成森林。

entries.definition: the restoration of plant cover of any kind, not necessarily trees.
entries.definitionCN: 植被恢复。恢复任何植物覆盖，不一定是树木。

entries.definition: the creation of new forest on bare or non-forest land; it is narrower than forestation.
entries.definitionCN: 新造林。在裸地或非林地上建立新林，比 forestation 窄。

entries.definition: the repair of a degraded forest's structure and function; it may involve natural regeneration, not only planting.
entries.definitionCN: 森林恢复。修复退化森林的结构与功能，可能依靠自然更新，而不只是栽植。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base is forest and the suffix -ation marks an action or its result.
normal.cn: 基础词是 forest，后缀 -ation 标记动作或结果。

normal.en: The technical pair is afforestation for new forest and reforestation for replanting.
normal.cn: 技术上的配对是：afforestation 指新造林，reforestation 指重新造林。

normal.en: Collocations: forestation program, forestation project, forestation rate.
normal.cn: 搭配：造林计划、造林项目、造林速度。

normal.en: Soil conservation and carbon policy are the two common policy frames.
normal.cn: 水土保持与碳政策是两种常见的政策框架。

normal.en: Forestation is the general word; tree planting is the everyday activity.
normal.cn: forestation 是总称；tree planting（植树）是日常活动。

abstract.en: Picture a bare slope marked out in rows before a single seedling goes in.
abstract.cn: 想象一片裸坡在栽下第一株苗之前就被划成一排排。

abstract.en: Picture a hillside turning from brown to green over ten annual photographs.
abstract.cn: 想象同一片山坡在十张年度照片里从褐色变成绿色。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where every hectare planted is entered as carbon stored.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，每栽一公顷就记下一笔碳储存。

examples.en: The forestation project aimed to stabilise sand dunes along the coast.
examples.cn: 这个造林项目旨在稳住沿海沙丘。

examples.en: Forestation of the catchment reduced erosion within five years.
examples.cn: 集水区造林在五年内减少了侵蚀。

examples.en: Carbon forestation is only credited if the new forest survives.
examples.cn: 只有新林存活，碳汇造林才被计入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森林 + 行动」——把一片地变成森林的整套动作 → 造林

root: 由 forest 加拉丁来源后缀 -ation 构成；forest 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 forestis。afforestation 与 reforestation 在十九至二十世纪成为更细的技术术语；具体年代为大致估计。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act at different stages and scales: the umbrella act, the slow process, the two technical subtypes, the program, the resulting area, the climate purpose and the land-use change.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一行为的不同阶段与尺度展开：总称行为、缓慢过程、两个技术子类、计划、结果面积、气候目的与土地用途改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare slope being turned into continuous green cover by deliberate planting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片裸坡通过有意栽植变成连续的绿色覆盖。

branches.en: ACT AND PROCESS: one deliberate act seen as an event and as a decade-long process.
branches.cn: 行为与过程：同一有意行为，既作事件看，也作十年过程看。

branches.en: TWO HISTORIES: new forest on bare land and replanting after loss.
branches.cn: 两种历史：裸地上的新林，与损失后的补植。

branches.en: SCALE AND RESULT: a program and the area it produces.
branches.cn: 规模与结果：计划以及它产生的面积。

branches.en: CLIMATE PURPOSE: the forest is planted to store carbon.
branches.cn: 气候目的：种林是为了储存碳。

branches.en: LAND-USE CHANGE: forest replaces another use and alters water and soil.
branches.cn: 土地用途改变：森林取代其他用途，并改变水土。

intro.en: Forestation is a transparent English formation: a borrowed base plus a Latin-derived action suffix, with technical subtypes added by prefixes.
intro.cn: forestation 是透明的英语构造：借入基础词加拉丁来源动作后缀，技术子类由前缀补充。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin forestis supplies forest; Latin -atio supplies -ation. The prefixes af- and re- create the two technical subtypes.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 forestis 提供 forest；拉丁语 -atio 提供 -ation。前缀 af- 与 re- 造出两个技术子类。

items.example: The forest gives shade and timber.

items.meaning: the act or result of establishing forest

items.example: The forestation rate doubled in five years.
items.exampleCN: 造林速度五年内翻了一倍。

items.meaning: new forest on land without recent forest
items.example: Afforestation changed the pasture to wood.
items.exampleCN: 新造林把牧场变成林地。

items.example: Restoration may rely on natural regeneration.
items.exampleCN: 森林恢复可能依靠自然更新。

definition_zh: 金属加工；金工：把已经提炼的金属切割、成形、连接并进行表面处理，制成器物或构件的手艺与工业
definition_en: the craft and industry of cutting, forming, joining and finishing metal into objects or parts
core_image: 一块平板金属被夹在台钳上，锯、锉、钻孔之后逐步变成一只带铰链的盒子
scene: 台面上摆着锯、锉、钻与焊枪，师傅把一块平板金属一步步做成带铰链的盒子。 Metalworking here still relies on hand tools more than on machines.
sceneCN: 这里指金属加工这门手艺整体（第 1 个义项：把金属材料加工成器物的工艺总称）；句意为这里的金属加工仍更多依靠手工工具，而不是机器。

pos.zh: 金属加工；金工（不可数，指工艺或行业总体）
（可数，指具体的加工活动或一次作业）

derivatives.zh: metal + work → 金工件；金属制品，语义偏移为「加工出来的物件」
metalworking + -er（从事者）→ 金工、金属加工工人
metal + ware（器皿）→ 金属器皿，语义偏移为「成套家用金属器具」
metal + smith（锻工）→ 金工师傅，语义偏移为「专做金属小件的匠人」
sheet（薄板）+ metalworking → 钣金加工，语义偏移为「以薄板为原料的成形工艺」

senses.title: The craft as a whole
senses.titleCN: 工艺总称：把金属变成器物的整套手艺
senses.definition: the whole craft of turning refined metal into useful objects
senses.definitionCN: 把精炼后的金属做成有用器物的整套手艺
senses.example: Metalworking here still relies on hand tools more than on machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的金属加工仍更多依靠手工工具，而不是机器。
senses.why: Metal leaves the smelter as a blank material; a second craft must give it shape, and the -ing form names that craft as one continuous activity rather than a single operation.
senses.whyCN: 金属从冶炼厂出来时只是一块空白材料；必须有第二门手艺给它形状，动名词形式把这门手艺说成一项持续的活动，而不是一个单独的操作。

senses.title: Cutting and forming
senses.titleCN: 切割与成形：锯、锉、车、铣、压
senses.definition: the operations that cut stock to size and shape it
senses.definitionCN: 把坯料切到尺寸并成形的各项操作
senses.example: Metalworking begins with measuring, marking and sawing the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 金属加工从量线、划线与锯板开始。
senses.why: Every later step depends on a clean cut and a true edge, so the craft's first skill is removing material exactly where it is not wanted.
senses.whyCN: 后面每一步都依赖干净的切口的准确边线，因此这门手艺的第一项本领，就是在不该有材料的地方精确地把它去掉。

senses.title: Joining and assembly
senses.titleCN: 连接与装配：焊接、铆接、螺栓固定
senses.definition: the operations that fasten separate pieces into one assembly
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的部件固定成一个整体的各项操作
senses.example: Metalworking includes welding, riveting and bolting.
senses.exampleCN: 金属加工包括焊接、铆接与螺栓连接。
senses.why: Once parts exist, they must be made to act as one body; heat, pressure or a fastener replaces the continuity that cutting destroyed.
senses.whyCN: 部件一旦存在，就必须让它们作为一个整体受力；热、压力或紧固件取代了切割所破坏的那种连续性。

senses.title: Finishing the surface
senses.titleCN: 表面处理与精饰：抛光、镀层、涂装
senses.definition: the operations that clean, polish, coat or otherwise finish a metal surface
senses.definitionCN: 对金属表面进行清洁、抛光、镀层或涂装的各项操作
senses.example: Final metalworking gives the sheet a brushed finish.
senses.exampleCN: 最后的金属加工给薄板做出拉丝表面。
senses.why: A surface is what a hand and an eye meet first, so the craft ends by controlling shine, texture and protection rather than shape.
senses.whyCN: 手和眼最先接触的是表面，因此这门手艺最后控制的是光泽、质感与防护，而不是形状。

senses.title: The shop
senses.titleCN: 作坊与车间：进行金工的场所
senses.definition: a workshop or bay where metal is worked
senses.definitionCN: 进行金属加工的作坊或车间
senses.example: The metalworking at the back of the yard was loud all day.
senses.exampleCN: 院子后面的金属加工车间整天都很吵。
senses.why: The activity's name transfers to the place built for it, because a shop is defined by the work done inside it.
senses.whyCN: 活动的名称转移到为它建造的场所，因为一个车间正是由里面所做的活计来定义的。

senses.title: A culture's metal craft
senses.titleCN: 历史与考古：某一文化的金属工艺
senses.definition: the metal craft of a place or period, studied from surviving objects and workshop waste
senses.definitionCN: 某一地点或时期的金属工艺，依据存世器物与作坊遗物研究
senses.example: Early metalworking in the region used native copper before any smelting.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区早期的金属加工在任何熔炼出现之前，先利用天然铜。
senses.why: Hammers, anvils and offcuts outlast the finished pieces, so a culture's craft can be reconstructed from the tools and scraps it left rather than from its treasures.
senses.whyCN: 锤子、砧子与边角料比成品存留得更久，因此一个文化的工艺可以从它留下的工具与碎料重建，而不是只靠珍品。

senses.title: The industry and the trade
senses.titleCN: 产业与职业：金属加工工业与工种
senses.definition: the sector that works metal commercially, and the occupation of those employed in it
senses.definitionCN: 以金属加工为业的产业部门，以及其中从业者的职业
senses.example: The metalworking sector employs more people than the smelter itself.
senses.exampleCN: 金属加工部门雇用的人比冶炼厂本身还多。
senses.why: A craft becomes an industry when its shops are counted together, and the same word then appears on payrolls, trade figures and training schemes.
senses.whyCN: 当众多作坊被合并计数，一门手艺就成了产业；同一个词随后出现在工资单、贸易数据与培训计划上。

senses.title: What comes out
senses.titleCN: 制品总体：加工出来的金属件
senses.definition: the collective output of metal parts and objects produced by the craft
senses.definitionCN: 这门手艺产出的金属件与器物的总体
senses.example: The museum's metalworking collection fills three rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的金属加工藏品占了三间展厅。
senses.why: Output can be named by the process that made it, so a shelf of hinges and brackets is spoken of as metalworking rather than as a list of parts.
senses.whyCN: 产出可以用制造它的过程来命名，于是一架铰链与托架被统称为金属加工品，而不是逐一列出零件。

intro.en: Metalworking is a transparent modern compound: an ancient borrowed noun for the material plus the oldest English verb for doing. Its parts are old, but the compound itself is modern.
intro.cn: metalworking 是一个透明的现代复合词：一个古老的借来名词指材料，加上英语最古老的动词之一表示「做」。部件很老，复合词本身却很新。

items.en: Metallon meant 'metal' and 'mine'. Its origin is uncertain, and the ancient connection with metalleuein 'to search after' explains the sense rather than proving the derivation.
items.cn: metallon 既指「金属」也指「矿」。它来源不确定，与 metalleuein「搜寻」的古老联系解释的是词义，而非证明了派生。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as metallum and passed it to French, from which Middle English took metal. The Latin form also gave metallic and metallurgy their first element.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词借作 metallum，再传给法语，中古英语从法语取来 metal。这个拉丁形式也为 metallic 与 metallurgy 提供了第一个成分。

items.en: Work goes back to Old English weorc, with cognates across the Germanic languages. Its Indo-European ancestry is reconstructed, so the deepest form is not attested.
items.cn: work 可追溯到古英语 weorc，在日耳曼诸语中有同族词。它更早的印欧来源属于重构，最深的形式并无记录。

items.en: Metal entered English in the Middle Ages through Old French metal, alongside the older native words for iron and steel; work already had both the noun and the verb senses it has today.
items.cn: metal 在中世纪经古法语进入英语，与指铁和钢的本族老词并存；work 当时已具备今天所有的名词与动词义。

items.en: The compound metalworking belongs to modern industrial writing; metalwork is recorded earlier as a word for worked metal and for the craft, and the -ing form grows with factory vocabulary in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: metalworking 这一复合词属于现代工业文献；metalwork 更早被记录，指加工过的金属与这门工艺，而动名词形式随十九世纪的工厂词汇一同壮大。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first recorded use of the exact compound is not fixed, and the etymology of the Greek word for metal remains unsettled in every reference that discusses it.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切复合词的最早书证没有定论，而希腊语「金属」一词的词源，在每一部讨论它的资料中都仍未解决。

note.en: Group one separates the close family forms; group two separates working metal from winning or studying it.
note.cn: 第一组把同族的近形词分开；第二组把加工金属与提取、研究金属分开。

entries.definition: The older noun for the craft and for worked metal as a class; metalworking stresses the activity and the industry.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的名词，指这门工艺或加工过的金属这一类东西；metalworking 更强调活动与产业。

entries.definition: The person who does the work; the -er ending marks the doer, not the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 做这项工作的人；-er 词尾标记做的人，而不是做的动作。

entries.definition: Metal household goods taken as a class; it names products, not the process that made them.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类的家用金属器皿；它命名产品，而不是制造产品的过程。

entries.definition: The extraction and refining of metal from ore; the metal must exist before metalworking can begin.
entries.definitionCN: 从矿石中提取与精炼金属；金属必须先存在，金属加工才能开始。

entries.definition: Working hot metal with hammer and anvil; it is the oldest branch of metalworking, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 用锤与砧加工热金属；它是金属加工最古老的一支，而不是全部。

entries.definition: Cutting metal with powered tools to precise dimensions; one operation inside metalworking.
entries.definitionCN: 用动力工具把金属切到精确尺寸；是金属加工内部的一项操作。

entries.definition: Building a structure from cut and joined pieces, often on site; it uses metalworking methods but adds assembly and erection.
entries.definitionCN: 用切好并连接好的部件造出结构，常在现场进行；它使用金属加工方法，但多了装配与安装。

entries.definition: Making parts by pouring molten metal into moulds; casting is a different route from cutting and hammering.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔融金属浇入铸型来造零件；铸造走的是与切割、锤打不同的路线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real words joined, a real family of forms, and stage words that mark the craft.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真词合成、一组真实的同族形式，以及标出这门手艺各阶段的词。

normal.en: metal + working: the compound simply says what is done to the material, which is why it needs no Latin suffix.
normal.cn: metal + working：这个复合词直接说出对材料做了什么，所以它不需要任何拉丁词尾。

normal.en: The family is regular: metalwork for the craft or the goods, metalworker for the person, metalware for the products.
normal.cn: 同族形式很规整：metalwork 指工艺或制品，metalworker 指人，metalware 指产品。

normal.en: The stage words are all real operations: sawing, filing, drilling, turning, welding, riveting, polishing.
normal.cn: 各阶段的词都是真实操作：锯、锉、钻、车、焊、铆、抛光。

normal.en: Its fixed phrases name the material and the place: sheet metalworking, metalworking shop, metalworking industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出材料与场所：钣金加工、金工作坊、金属加工工业。

normal.en: The contrast to remember is with metallurgy: winning metal from rock versus shaping metal already won.
normal.cn: 要记住的对比是与 metallurgy：从石头里取金属，对比把取来的金属做成形。

abstract.en: Picture a flat sheet as a sentence that the craft rewrites by removing, joining and polishing.
abstract.cn: 想象一块平板是一句话，这门手艺通过去掉、连接与打磨来改写它。

abstract.en: Picture four rooms in a row: one cuts, one joins, one smooths, one checks the shine.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的四个房间：一间在切，一间在接，一间在磨，一间在看光泽。

abstract.en: Picture the same workshop seen twice, once as a noisy bay and once as a museum shelf of hinges.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个作坊看两次：一次是吵闹的车间，一次是博物馆里摆满铰链的架子。

examples.en: Sheet metalworking turns flat stock into ducts and casings.
examples.cn: 钣金加工把平板坯料做成风管与外壳。

examples.en: Metalworking tools were among the first objects buried with their owners.
examples.cn: 金工工具是最早与主人一同下葬的物件之一。

examples.en: The metalworking shop makes brackets for the same factory it supplies.
examples.cn: 这家金工作坊为它所供货的那家工厂制作托架。

dict_mnemonic.text: metal（金属）+ working（加工）＝ 金属加工；记「先切、再成形、再连接、最后抛光」。

root: metal 来自希腊 metallon「金属、矿」，经拉丁 metallum 与古法语进入英语；working 来自古英语 weorc「劳作」。两词合用，指金属成形的手艺。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the stock: it is cut, formed, joined and finished, and the work also names a shop, a culture, an industry and its output.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着坯料走：被切、成形、连接、精饰；这门活计又命名了车间、一种文化、一个产业以及它的产出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flat stock is measured, cut, bent, joined and polished until it is a finished object.
core.cn: 核心意象：平板坯料被量、切、弯、接、磨，直到成为一件成品。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: the whole second stage that begins after the metal is already refined.
branches.cn: 手艺整体：金属精炼之后才开始的整个第二阶段。

branches.en: TAKING MATERIAL AWAY AND PUTTING IT TOGETHER: cutting and forming, then welding and fastening.
branches.cn: 去掉材料与把材料接上：先切割成形，再焊接紧固。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: polishing and coating, where the eye and the hand meet the object.
branches.cn: 表面：抛光与镀层，手和眼在这里接触器物。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND THE PAST: a noisy shop here, a reconstructed craft tradition there.
branches.cn: 场所与过去：一边是吵闹的车间，一边是被重建的工艺传统。

branches.en: THE SCALE AND THE OUTPUT: a whole sector with payrolls, and the parts that come out of it.
branches.cn: 规模与产出：一个有工资单的完整部门，以及从中出来的零件。

intro.en: The compound is built from a borrowed noun and a native verb, and both halves take ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由借来的名词与本族动词搭成，两半都接普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes only the material word, metallum, borrowed in turn from Greek; the working half is native English, so the compound is mixed in origin by design.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只贡献了材料词 metallum（它又借自希腊语）；「加工」那一半是英语本族词，因此这个复合词在来源上本来就是混合的。

items.structure: metal (n., from Old French, from Latin metallum, from Greek metallon)
items.meaning: a hard shiny material such as iron or copper
items.meaningCN: 铁、铜一类坚硬有光泽的材料
items.example: The metal is delivered as flat sheet.
items.exampleCN: 金属以平板形式送进车间。

items.structure: work (native verb and noun, Old English weorc)

items.example: They work the sheet by hand.

the craft, or worked metal as a class

items.exampleCN: 这扇门是精细的金工件。

items.example: The metalworker marked the plate before cutting.
items.exampleCN: 金工在切之前先在板上划线。

items.meaning: metal household goods as a class
items.meaningCN: 作为一类的金属家用器具
items.example: The stall sells brass and copper metalware.

items.meaning: working thin flat metal into shapes
items.meaningCN: 把金属薄板加工成各种形状
items.exampleCN: 钣金加工造出这些风管。

items.meaningCN: 金属成形的手艺与产业

definition_zh: 威吓；欺凌；吓唬（迫使屈服）
definition_en: to intimidate someone into doing something by stern or bullying looks and words
core_image: 压低的眉毛像乌云，逼人低头
scene: 会议室里，上司瞪着眼一遍遍逼人签字。 The manager browbeat the clerk into signing the unequal contract.
sceneCN: 这里 browbeat 是「威吓、欺凌」（第 1 个义项：以凶狠的言辞神色逼人屈服）；句意是经理威逼职员签下不平等合同。

pos.zh: 威吓；欺凌；逼（某人）就范

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「被威吓的，逆来顺受的」
由现在分词转名词，义为「威吓，欺压」

senses.title: To intimidate into submission
senses.definition: to use stern looks and harsh words to force someone to give in
senses.definitionCN: 以严厉的神色和粗暴的言辞迫使某人让步
senses.example: The lawyer browbeat the witness into changing her answer.
senses.exampleCN: 律师威吓证人，逼她改口。
senses.why: The brow is the face of anger; beating down with the brow pictures a scowl that crushes resistance.
senses.whyCN: 眉毛（brow）是怒容所在，用「眉毛压打」描摹一副凶相把对方的反抗压垮。

senses.title: To bully habitually
senses.definition: to treat someone in a domineering, bullying way as a habit
senses.definitionCN: 习惯性地以颐指气使的方式欺压他人
senses.example: He browbeat his younger colleagues for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他多年来一直盛气凌人地欺负年轻同事。
senses.why: A repeated act of intimidation hardens into a manner of dealing with people.
senses.whyCN: 一次次的威吓累积成一种惯常待人方式，义项由动作转为作风。

senses.title: To hector in debate
senses.definition: to shout down or overbear an opponent in argument rather than reason with them
senses.definitionCN: 在争论中用声势压倒对方，而非以理服人
senses.example: The senator browbeat his rival instead of answering the question.
senses.exampleCN: 参议员不回答问题，只顾气势汹汹地压对手。
senses.why: When force of expression replaces force of argument, intimidation becomes a rhetorical weapon.
senses.whyCN: 当表达上的强势取代论据的力量，威吓便成了论辩武器，义项延伸到言辞交锋。

intro.en: Browbeat is an English compound: brow plus beat, first recorded in the late sixteenth century.
intro.cn: browbeat 是英语复合词：brow 加 beat，十六世纪末见于记载。

items.en: a reconstructed root bhru gave the word for the brow or eyebrow.
items.cn: 重构词根 bhru 演变出表示眉、额的词。

items.en: brū appeared for the brow, while bēatan meant to strike.
items.cn: 古英语 brū 指眉毛，bēatan 意为击打。

items.en: browbeat arose as a figure: to beat down with a scowling brow.
items.cn: browbeat 作为比喻产生：以怒眉压人、以凶相逼人。

items.en: the past participle browbeaten settled as the common form, meaning cowed.
items.cn: 过去分词 browbeaten 定型，表「被吓住的」。

items.en: browbeat now names any bullying by looks, tone or pressure.
items.cn: 如今 browbeat 泛指以神色、语气或压力欺凌逼人。

note.en: Browbeat keeps company with body-part verbs of intimidation and with near synonyms of bullying.
note.cn: browbeat 与身体部位构成的威慑类动词以及欺凌近义词相伴。

entries.definition: the strip of hair above the eye
entries.definitionCN: 眉毛，与 browbeat 同含 brow 一词

entries.definition: to strike repeatedly
entries.definitionCN: 击打，browbeat 的第二成分

entries.definition: to mix or whip too much
entries.definitionCN: 搅拌过度，只是形近，与威吓义无关

entries.definition: to frighten someone into doing something
entries.definitionCN: 恐吓，威吓，与 browbeat 义近

entries.definition: to treat someone cruelly and repeatedly
entries.definitionCN: 欺凌，恃强凌弱

entries.definition: to frighten someone into obedience
entries.definitionCN: 吓住，使畏缩

entries.definition: to bully in an arrogant way
entries.definitionCN: 威吓，盛气凌人

entries.definition: to make someone lose courage
entries.definitionCN: 使胆怯，使气馁

normalIntro.en: Picture a scowling brow doing the beating instead of a fist.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一双怒眉在动手打人，而非拳头。

normal.en: brow means the forehead; beat here means to strike down.
normal.cn: brow 指眉额，beat 在此指压打。

normal.en: The image is a scowl strong enough to knock you down.
normal.cn: 意象是一道凶得能把人打倒的怒容。

normal.en: The common participle is browbeaten, like beaten but with brows.
normal.cn: 常见分词是 browbeaten，像 beaten 但换成了眉毛。

normal.en: Browbeat someone into something is the fixed pattern.
normal.cn: browbeat someone into something 是固定句式。

normal.en: Bully uses fists; browbeat uses only the face.
normal.cn: bully 动拳头，browbeat 只用脸色。

abstract.en: Feel a shadow lean over you until your shoulders shrink.
abstract.cn: 感受一道阴影俯压过来，肩头不由收缩。

abstract.en: See two dark eyebrows slide lower and lower.
abstract.cn: 看见两道黑眉越压越低。

abstract.en: Hear a voice grind down every reply you start.
abstract.cn: 听一个声音把你开口的每句回话碾碎。

examples.en: The witness said she had been browbeaten by the prosecutor.
examples.cn: 证人说她曾被检察官威吓。

examples.en: Sales teams should coach, not browbeat, their trainees.
examples.cn: 销售团队应辅导新人，而非威压。

examples.en: He refused to be browbeaten into signing the deal.
examples.cn: 他拒绝在威逼下签署协议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不饶比特」——他瞪着眉毛「不饶」人，一点「比特」的温和都没有，纯靠凶相压人。

root: browbeat 由 brow（眉、额，上溯原始印欧语重构词根 bhru）加 beat（打，古英语 bēatan）复合而成，属英语本土比喻构词：以「怒眉压打」表示用凶狠神色逼人屈服，无拉丁词源。

sensesIntro.en: One scowl that crushes resistance widens into a habit of bullying and then into overbearing debate.
sensesIntro.cn: 一道压垮反抗的怒容，先固化为惯常欺压，再延伸到论辩中的以势压人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scowling brow pressing down like a fist.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道怒眉像拳头般压下。

branches.en: browbeat a witness
branches.cn: 威吓证人

branches.en: browbeat an opponent in debate
branches.cn: 论辩中以势压人

branches.en: a browbeating manager
branches.cn: 惯于威压的主管

branches.en: refuse to be browbeaten
branches.cn: 拒不屈服于威吓

branches.en: a browbeaten staff
branches.cn: 被压得不敢说话的员工

intro.en: Browbeat is a verb compound: a body part acts as the weapon.
intro.cn: browbeat 是动词复合词：身体部位充当「凶器」。

latinIntro.en: The compound is Germanic, but brow has distant Latin cousins in words like supercilium.
latinIntro.cn: 复合结构属日耳曼语源，brow 的远亲可见于拉丁语 supercilium（眉，引申傲慢）。

items.example: wipe the sweat from his brow

definition_zh: adj. 自夸的，爱吹嘘的
definition_en: talking too proudly about your own deeds, possessions or abilities
core_image: 一个人说着说着就把话题转回自己那辆车
scene: 他每三句话就要提一次自己那辆新车。 He was boastful, mentioning his new car every third sentence.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：boastful 指爱自夸；句意是他每三句话就要提一次自己的新车。

pos.zh: 自夸的；爱吹嘘的

forms.label: 形容词原级（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Praising oneself too much
senses.definition: speaking with too much pride about one own actions or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 对自己的行为或品性表现出过分自豪
senses.example: His boastful account of the match left out the lost set.
senses.exampleCN: 他对比赛的吹嘘漏掉了输掉的那一盘。
senses.why: The suffix -ful means full of, so boastful is simply full of boasting.
senses.whyCN: -ful 意为充满，boastful 就是「充满自夸」。

senses.title: Showing off what one owns
senses.definition: drawing attention to possessions in a way meant to impress others
senses.definitionCN: 以引人注目的方式展示自己的财物
senses.example: A boastful watch is still just a watch.
senses.exampleCN: 一块炫耀用的表，终究只是一块表。
senses.why: Boasting began with words about deeds and spread to objects held up for admiration.
senses.whyCN: 自夸本是对功绩的言语，后来扩展到被举起来求赞美的物件。

intro.en: Boastful is boast plus -ful; boast itself appears in the thirteenth century with an uncertain origin.
intro.cn: boastful 是 boast 加 -ful；boast 本身十三世纪已见，来源不确定。

items.en: Middle English bost means a loud threat or display.
items.cn: 中古英语 bost 意为高声恐吓或炫示。

items.en: No source for boast has been proved.
items.cn: boast 的来源未获证实。

items.en: The word shifts from threat to praising oneself.
items.cn: 这个词由恐吓转为自我夸耀。

items.en: Boastful appears as the adjective of being full of boasts.
items.cn: boastful 作为「充满自夸」的形容词出现。

items.en: The word becomes a common judgement of character.
items.cn: 这个词成为常见的品性评价。

items.en: Boastful now covers words and possessions alike.
items.cn: 现代 boastful 兼指言语与所有物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ful ending or the b- stem; the near-meaning group ranks pride from confident to insufferable.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ful 词尾或 b- 词干；近义组把骄傲从自信排到令人难忍。

entries.definition: To talk proudly about oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 自豪地谈论自己。

entries.definition: To raise or improve something.
entries.definitionCN: 提高；促进。

entries.definition: Shy and easily embarrassed.
entries.definitionCN: 害羞易窘的。

entries.definition: Large in amount, generous.
entries.definitionCN: 丰盛的；慷慨的。

entries.definition: Feeling superior to other people.
entries.definitionCN: 自视高于他人。

entries.definition: Having too high an opinion of oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己评价过高。

entries.definition: Too proud of one looks or qualities.
entries.definitionCN: 过分看重外表或优点。

entries.definition: Showing too high an opinion of oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己评价过高、不加收敛。

normalIntro.en: Boast plus -ful: a person so full of boasting that it spills into every conversation.
normalIntro.cn: boast 加 -ful：一个人自夸得太满，溢出到每段谈话里。

normal.en: -ful means full of, as in hopeful and careful.
normal.cn: -ful 意为充满，如 hopeful、careful。

normal.en: So boastful means full of boasts.
normal.cn: 所以 boastful 就是「充满自夸」。

normal.en: The boastful guest turns every topic to himself.
normal.cn: 自夸的客人把每个话题都转回自己。

normal.en: Boasting began as loud threat, then became bragging.
normal.cn: 自夸原是高声恐吓，后来变成吹嘘。

normal.en: A watch can be boastful too, if it is held up.
normal.cn: 表如果被举起来展示，也可以很「自夸」。

abstract.en: A sentence that always ends at I.
abstract.cn: 总是落在「我」上的一句话。

abstract.en: Praise borrowed from oneself.
abstract.cn: 向自己借来的赞美。

abstract.en: A story with only one hero.
abstract.cn: 只有一个英雄的故事。

examples.en: He grew boastful after the promotion.
examples.cn: 升职之后他变得爱自夸了。

examples.en: Her boastful emails did not impress the client.
examples.cn: 她那些自夸的邮件并没有打动客户。

examples.en: It was a boastful claim, but the figures backed it.
examples.cn: 那话说得夸口，不过数字支持它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不求是」——自夸的人只求说得响，不求是不是真的。

root: boast（自夸）+ -ful（充满……的）

sensesIntro.en: The first sense is about words, the second about objects; both are the same wish to be admired.
sensesIntro.cn: 第一义关于言语，第二义关于物件；两者都是同一种「求人称赞」的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every topic bending back to the speaker own car
core.cn: 核心意象：每个话题都拐回说话人自己的车

branches.en: A match report with the lost set missing.
branches.cn: 漏掉输掉那盘的比赛叙述。

branches.en: A story that ends at I.
branches.cn: 以「我」收尾的故事。

branches.en: A watch turned to catch the light.
branches.cn: 被转过来反光的表。

branches.en: Keys left on the table.
branches.cn: 故意留在桌上的钥匙。

branches.en: Words and objects asking for praise.
branches.cn: 求赞的言语与物件。

intro.en: Boastful is a stem plus a very common adjective suffix; the list below builds its family and other -ful words with the same shape.
intro.cn: boastful 是词干加一个极常见的形容词词尾；下面列出它的词族与同形的其他 -ful 词。

latinIntro.en: Latin iactare means to throw out boasts, glorificare to glorify, and superbus proud.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iactare 意为抛出自夸，glorificare 意为颂扬，superbus 意为傲慢。

latinEntries.exampleCN: iactare 产生 jet 与 ejaculate。
superbus 是 superb 的来源。

definition_zh: 肖像画艺术；肖像画（总称）；人像摄影
definition_en: the art or practice of making portraits, or portraits considered as a group
core_image: 许多张脸在同一面墙上排开，构成一种看人的传统
scene: 美术馆把四个世纪的肖像排成一条线索，从木板画一直排到照片。 The exhibition traces four centuries of portraiture, from panel painting to photography.
sceneCN: 这里 portraiture 指「肖像创作这门艺术及其历史实践」（第 1 个义项：制作肖像的艺术）；句意为展览梳理四个世纪的肖像艺术，从木板画直到摄影。

pos.zh: 肖像画艺术；肖像画总称（通常不可数）

forms.label: 可数用法（少见，指多种实践）

derivatives.zh: portraiture 逆构 → 单幅肖像；从「整体实践」转到「一件作品」
portrait + -ist（人）→ 肖像作者；从「实践」转到「从业者」
self- + portraiture → 自我肖像实践；从「他人」转到「自我」

senses.title: The art of making portraits
senses.definition: the art, skill or practice of making portraits
senses.definitionCN: 制作肖像的艺术、技巧或实践
senses.example: The exhibition traces four centuries of portraiture.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览梳理四个世纪的肖像艺术。
senses.why: The suffix -ure, from Latin -ura, names an activity and its result; added to portrait, it turns one work into the practice that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ure 来自拉丁 -ura，命名活动及其结果；加在 portrait 上，就把单件作品变成生产它的实践。

senses.title: Portraits considered as a group
senses.definition: portraits collectively, especially in a collection or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 肖像作品的集合，尤指一个收藏或传统中的总体
senses.example: The castle's portraiture fills three galleries.
senses.exampleCN: 城堡的肖像藏品装满三个展厅。
senses.why: An uncountable mass noun treats many works as one body, the way furniture gathers many objects.
senses.whyCN: 不可数集合名词把许多作品当作一个整体，正如 furniture 收拢许多物件。

senses.title: A single portrait, in older use
senses.definition: one portrait, a countable use now largely replaced by portrait
senses.definitionCN: 一幅肖像；这一可数用法现在大多被 portrait 取代
senses.example: The inventory lists a portraiture of the duke.
senses.exampleCN: 清单上列有一幅公爵肖像。
senses.why: Before the back-formed portrait spread, portraiture could still mean one picture; the newer word took over the count.
senses.whyCN: 在逆构的 portrait 普及之前，portraiture 仍可指一幅画；较新的词接管了计数功能。

senses.title: A literary portrayal
senses.definition: a description or portrayal of a person in writing
senses.definitionCN: 文字中对一个人的描写或刻画
senses.example: The chapter is a portraiture of the family in one long evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章以漫长的一夜刻画了这个家庭。
senses.why: The metaphor of painting extends to writing: a text can be called a portraiture when it builds a person detail by detail.
senses.whyCN: 绘画的隐喻扩展到写作：当文本逐笔构建一个人物时，就可以被称为一幅 portraiture。

senses.title: The genre in art history
senses.definition: portrait-making as a recognised genre of art
senses.definitionCN: 作为受认可艺术门类的肖像制作
senses.example: Portraiture was ranked below history painting.
senses.exampleCN: 肖像画在等级上低于历史画。
senses.why: Once a practice is classified, its name becomes a genre label in academies and museums.
senses.whyCN: 一旦实践被分类，其名称就成为学院与博物馆中的门类标签。

senses.title: A style or approach within the genre
senses.titleCN: 肖像门类中的风格或路径
senses.definition: a distinctive manner or approach to making portraits
senses.definitionCN: 制作肖像的独特方式或路径
senses.example: Her portraiture avoids the frontal stare.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肖像手法回避正面直视。
senses.why: A practice can be done in different ways, so the mass noun also names a manner, not only the category.
senses.whyCN: 同一实践可以有不同做法，因此这个集合名词也命名一种手法，而不只是类别。

senses.title: The commissioning business
senses.definition: the social and commercial system of commissioning portraits
senses.definitionCN: 委托制作肖像的社会与商业体系
senses.example: Eighteenth-century portraiture depended on aristocratic commissions.
senses.exampleCN: 18 世纪的肖像业依赖贵族委托。
senses.why: Portraits cost money and mark status, so the practice also names the economy of patrons and sitters.
senses.whyCN: 肖像耗资且标示身份，因此这门实践也命名赞助人与被画者构成的经济。

senses.title: Photographic portrait practice
senses.definition: the practice of making portraits with a camera
senses.definitionCN: 用相机制作肖像的实践
senses.example: Studio portraiture moved from painted backdrops to paper rolls.
senses.exampleCN: 影室人像从手绘背景转到纸卷背景。
senses.why: When the camera took over the likeness, the old practice word went with it and named a new medium's version.
senses.whyCN: 当相机接管肖像制作，旧的实践名词也随之而去，命名新媒介中的版本。

intro.en: Portraiture came into English from Old French in the late fourteenth century, from the same verb that gives portray and portrait. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: portraiture 于 14 世纪后期从古法语进入英语，与 portray、portrait 同出一个动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Protrahere 'to draw forth' joined pro- 'forth' and trahere 'to draw'; medieval Latin used it for painting as well as revealing.
items.cn: protrahere「拉出、描绘」由 pro-「向前」与 trahere「拉」组合；中世纪拉丁也用它指绘画，而不只是显露。

items.en: Old French portraire meant 'to draw, paint, portray'; its noun forms supplied both portrait and portraiture.
items.cn: 古法语 portraire 意为「画、描绘」；其名词形式同时提供 portrait 与 portraiture。

items.en: Old French portraiture (twelfth century) meant 'portrait, image, portrayal, resemblance'.
items.cn: 古法语 portraiture（12 世纪）意为「肖像、形象、描绘、相似」。

items.en: English portraiture is recorded in the late fourteenth century for 'the art of making portraits; a painting or drawing'.
items.cn: 英语 portraiture 于 14 世纪后期有记录，指「制作肖像的艺术；一幅绘画或素描」。

items.en: The countable sense 'a portrait' passed to the back-formed portrait in the sixteenth century, leaving portraiture for the art and the collective.
items.cn: 可数义「一幅肖像」在 16 世纪转给逆构的 portrait，portraiture 则保留给艺术与总称。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century photography extended the practice word to camera portraits without changing its core meaning.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪的摄影把这一实践名词扩展到相机肖像，核心意义未变。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words that differ in count or word class; group two holds labels for the practice seen from other trades.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、但计数或词类不同的词；第二组是从其他行当看待这门实践的标签。

entries.definition: A single likeness; portraiture is the practice or the whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 单件形象；portraiture 是实践或整体。

entries.definition: A maker of portraits; the ending -ist names the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 肖像制作者；词尾 -ist 命名从业者。

entries.definition: To depict a person or scene; portraiture is the resulting practice noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描绘人物或场景；portraiture 是相应的实践名词。

entries.definition: The practice of making portraits of oneself; the compound adds self to the practice word.
entries.definitionCN: 制作自我肖像的实践；复合词在实践名词前加了 self。

entries.definition: Portrait-making in paint specifically; portraiture also covers photography, sculpture and drawing.
entries.definitionCN: 特指用颜料制作肖像；portraiture 还涵盖摄影、雕塑与素描。

entries.definition: The act of representing anything in image or words; portraiture is limited to persons and their likeness.
entries.definitionCN: 以图像或文字再现任何事物的行为；portraiture 限于人物及其形象。

entries.definition: The quality of resembling someone, or an image that does so; portraiture is the organised practice of producing such images.
entries.definitionCN: 相似的性质，或相似的形象；portraiture 是生产此类图像的成体系实践。

entries.definition: Image-making with light; photographic portraiture is one branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 用光成像；人像摄影是其中的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: portrait + -ure: the activity and its accumulated result.
normal.cn: portrait + -ure：活动及其累积结果。

normal.en: The word came through Old French portraiture from portraire, 'to draw forth'.
normal.cn: 这个词经古法语 portraiture 来自 portraire「向前描出」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the practice: the art of portraiture, British portraiture, commissioned portraiture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出实践：肖像艺术、英国肖像画、委托肖像创作。

normal.en: The family runs portrait, portraits, portraitist, portray and self-portraiture.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 portrait、portraits、portraitist、portray 与 self-portraiture。

normal.en: The -ure ending also appears in literature and furniture, both mass-like nouns of activity or result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ure 也出现在 literature 与 furniture 中，都是偏集合的活动或结果名词。

abstract.en: Picture many faces lined up until they become one tradition.
abstract.cn: 想象许多张脸排成一行，直到变成一种传统。

abstract.en: Picture a practice that outlives every sitter it depicts.
abstract.cn: 想象一门比它所描绘的每位被画者都活得久的实践。

abstract.en: Picture a verb, a single work and a whole wall sharing one root.
abstract.cn: 想象一个动词、一件作品与一整面墙共享同一个词根。

examples.en: Portraiture was the academy's steadiest source of income.
examples.cn: 肖像画是学院最稳定的收入来源。

examples.en: The book surveys portraiture from panel to screen.
examples.cn: 这本书梳理从木板到屏幕的肖像实践。

examples.en: Her portraiture gives equal weight to hands and faces.
examples.cn: 她的肖像手法给手与脸同等的分量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「portrait（肖像）+ -ure（行为/结果）」——画肖像这件事 → 肖像画艺术

root: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」经古法语 portraire 与名词 portraiture（12 世纪），14 世纪后期进入英语，指制作肖像的艺术；16 世纪单数义转给 portrait。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the art itself to the collective body, the older single picture, the literary portrayal, the genre, a style, the commissioning economy and photographic practice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从艺术本身转到作品总称、较早的单幅用法、文学刻画、门类、风格、委托经济与摄影实践。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many faces are lined up on one wall until they form a way of looking at people.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多张脸在同一面墙上排开，直到构成一种看人的方式。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE AND ITS PURSE: making portraits, and the commissions that pay for them.
branches.cn: 实践及其钱袋：制作肖像，以及为此付费的委托。

branches.en: MANY AND ONE: the collective body, then the older countable single picture.
branches.cn: 多与一：作品总称，然后是较早的可数单幅用法。

branches.en: IN WORDS: the practice borrowed for literary character-building.
branches.cn: 文字之中：这门实践被借去构建文学人物。

branches.en: GENRE AND MANNER: the category, then a distinctive way of working inside it.
branches.cn: 门类与手法：先是类别，再是类别内独特的工作方式。

branches.en: THE CAMERA: the same practice in a new medium.
branches.cn: 相机：同一实践在新媒介中的形态。

intro.en: Portraiture is a French noun of action and result; its ending is no longer productive in English, but the root family still is.
intro.cn: portraiture 是法语的动作与结果名词；其词尾在英语中已不再能产，但词根词族仍能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin protrahere and trahere are the deep sources; French supplied the -ure noun shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protrahere 与 trahere 是深层来源；法语提供 -ure 的名词形态。

items.example: The prefix adds the sense of drawing out.
The root also gives trace and tractor.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还给出 trace 与 tractor。
这个动词成为英语 portray。

items.example: Literature and furniture use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: literature 与 furniture 用同一个词尾。

items.structure: French past participle used as noun
items.example: The portrait is signed on the back.

items.exampleCN: 这位肖像画家偏爱粉笔。

items.example: Self-portraiture runs through his late work.
items.exampleCN: 自我肖像贯穿他晚期的作品。

definition_zh: 程序的；程序性的；手续上的；（法律）程序法的；按步骤操作的
definition_en: relating to the steps or rules by which something is done, rather than to its substance or result
core_image: 一张按序号排好的流程图贴在墙上，每一步都用箭头连到下一步
scene: 法官没有讨论谁更有理，而是先问警方取证时是否按规定的步骤通知了当事人。 The court raised a procedural question about whether the search had followed the required steps.
sceneCN: 这里指与程序、步骤有关的（第 2 个义项：法律程序上的）；句意为法院提出了一个程序问题，即这次搜查是否按规定的步骤进行。场景图取象：墙上贴着按序号排好的流程图。

pos.zh: 程序的；程序性的
（法律）程序法的；与程序有关的
（计算机）过程式的；按步骤展开的

derivatives.zh: 程序；步骤；手续（由表示「向前走」的拉丁动词加名词词尾构成，指一步步走的路径）
在程序上；按程序地（加副词词尾，指从程序角度看）
继续进行；行进（同源动词，字面即「向前走」，是 procedure 的动作基础）
诉讼程序；会议记录（现在分词转名词，指正在进行的一系列步骤）
过程；处理（同出「向前走」的拉丁词根，但走的是另一条名词化路径）
程序主义（在形容词后加表示「学说、倾向」的后缀，指重视程序的立场）

senses.title: Belonging to the steps
senses.definition: relating to the way in which something is done, rather than to what is done
senses.definitionCN: 关涉做事的方式与步骤，而非所做之事的内容
senses.example: The change was procedural, not a matter of policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这一改动是程序上的，不涉及政策本身。
senses.why: The base noun procedure names a path walked step by step, so the adjective marks the path rather than the destination.
senses.whyCN: 基础名词指一步步走过的路径，因此这个形容词标的是路径而非终点。

senses.title: Of the rules of court
senses.definition: concerning the rules that govern how a legal case is conducted
senses.definitionCN: 关于主导案件如何审理的规则的
senses.example: The appeal was lost on procedural grounds.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉因程序上的理由而失败。
senses.why: Law separates substance from procedure, and the adjective names the second half of that split.
senses.whyCN: 法律把实体与程序分开，这个形容词指这一划分的后一半。

senses.title: Fair in the way it is done
senses.definition: describing fairness in the process itself, such as being heard before a decision
senses.definitionCN: 指过程本身的公正，例如在决定之前有陈述的机会
senses.example: Procedural fairness required the board to hear both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 程序公正要求委员会听取双方意见。
senses.why: A good result reached by a bad path is still suspect, so fairness attaches to the steps.
senses.whyCN: 用坏路径得到的好结果仍然可疑，所以公正落在步骤上。

senses.title: Safeguards against error
senses.definition: of rules designed to catch mistakes, such as a second reading or a signature
senses.definitionCN: 指为发现错误而设的规则，如二次审读或签名确认
senses.example: The agency added procedural checks before approving loans.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构在批准贷款前增加了程序性核查。
senses.why: Bureaucracy is often defended as a set of small procedural brakes on haste.
senses.whyCN: 官僚程序常被辩护为一组对仓促行事的小小刹车。

senses.title: Step-by-step in computing
senses.definition: of a programming style built from named sequences of instructions, as opposed to object-oriented style
senses.definitionCN: 指由命名的指令序列构成的编程风格，与面向对象风格相对
senses.example: The course starts with procedural programming in a simple language.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从简单语言的过程式编程讲起。
senses.why: Software borrowed the word for code that reads like a list of steps to be walked through.
senses.whyCN: 软件领域借这个词指读起来像一串待走步骤的代码。

senses.title: Of a parliamentary motion
senses.definition: concerning the conduct of a meeting, such as a motion on speaking time
senses.definitionCN: 关于会议如何进行的，如关于发言时间的动议
senses.example: The chair ruled the objection procedural and set it aside.
senses.exampleCN: 主席裁定这一异议属程序问题，暂不处理。
senses.why: Assemblies run on rules of order, and a procedural motion keeps the argument about the rules.
senses.whyCN: 议会依议事规则运转，程序性动议把争论留在规则层面。

senses.title: Characteristic of a procedure
senses.definition: having the character of a routine, done in a fixed order without much judgement
senses.definitionCN: 带有例行程序的特征，按固定次序执行而少有判断
senses.example: The interview felt procedural, with the same questions for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这场面谈显得很程序化，每个人都问同样的问题。
senses.why: When a human act becomes a fixed sequence, the adjective moves from describing rules to describing behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 当人的行为变成固定序列，这个形容词就从描述规则转为描述举止。

senses.title: Of medical procedures
senses.definition: relating to a medical or surgical procedure rather than to diagnosis alone
senses.definitionCN: 关涉医疗或外科操作本身，而非仅指诊断
senses.example: The clinic offers procedural sedation for minor surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所的小手术提供操作中的镇静。
senses.why: Medicine names by procedure what is done with hands, and the adjective separates it from talk and tests.
senses.whyCN: 医学以操作命名动手做的事，这个形容词把它与谈话和检查分开。

intro.en: Procedural is procedure plus -al. Procedure comes from Latin procedere 'to go forward', from pro- 'forward' and cedere 'to go'. The line is clear; the exact date of the adjective in English is uncertain.
intro.cn: procedural 是 procedure 加 -al。procedure 出自拉丁语 procedere「向前走」，由 pro-「向前」与 cedere「走」构成。线索清楚，这个形容词进入英语的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Cedere meant to go, to yield or to give way, and it stands behind proceed, process and succeed.
items.cn: cedere 意为走、让步或退让，proceed、process 与 succeed 都由它而来。

items.en: Procedere combined the forward prefix with that verb to mean to go forward, to advance, to come out.
items.cn: procedere 把表示向前的前缀与这个动词结合，意为前行、推进、走出。

items.en: Old French procedure named the manner of conducting a case, a word of courts before it was a word of offices.
items.cn: 古法语的 procedure 指审理案件的方式，先是法庭用语，后成公务用语。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the sixteenth century, first in law and then in general administration.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个名词，先用于法律，随后用于一般行政。

items.en: The adjective followed, and modern law fixed the contrast between procedural and substantive rules.
items.cn: 形容词随后出现，现代法律确立了程序规则与实体规则的对立。

items.en: In the later twentieth century the adjective was applied to programming built from named steps.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，这个形容词被用来指由命名步骤构成的编程方式。

note.en: The first group shares the going-forward root or looks close; the second group holds words that describe rules and steps but are not the same contrast.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「向前走」词根，或字形相近；第二组描述规则与步骤，却不是同一个对立面。

entries.definition: The noun: a set of steps for doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：做事的一套步骤。

entries.definition: To go on or move forward, the verb inside the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 继续或向前走，是名词里的动词。

entries.definition: A course of action, often in the plural for legal or formal business.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列行动，复数多指法律或正式事务。

entries.definition: A series of changes; it shares cedere through a different Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列变化；经另一个拉丁名词共享同一词根。

entries.definition: Wastefully generous; it looks like the same prefix but comes from a verb meaning to squander.
entries.definitionCN: 挥霍的；前缀看似相同，词根却意为耗费。

entries.definition: Following established rules, which often overlaps with procedural but concerns form.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循既定规则，常与程序重叠，但着眼在形式。

entries.definition: Concerning the running of an organisation rather than its policy.
entries.definitionCN: 关涉机构运转而非政策。

entries.definition: A fixed sequence of actions with symbolic weight, closer to ceremony than to rule.
entries.definitionCN: 带象征分量的固定动作序列，更近仪式而非规则。

entries.definition: Done by an ordered plan, emphasising method rather than rules.
entries.definitionCN: 按有序计划进行，强调方法而非规则。

entries.definition: Concerning the actual rights and duties at issue, the opposite half of the legal split.
entries.definitionCN: 关涉争议中的实际权利与义务，是法律划分的另一半。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real going-forward root, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「向前走」词根、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Cedere means to go, and procedere means to go forward, so a procedure is a path walked step by step.
normal.cn: 词根意为走，加向前的前缀即前行，程序就是一步步走过的路径。

normal.en: The family runs proceed, procedure, proceeding, procedural and process.
normal.cn: 同族词有 proceed、procedure、proceeding、procedural 与 process。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: procedural rules, procedural fairness, procedural law, procedural error.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：程序规则、程序公正、程序法、程序性错误。

normal.en: Law divides the world into procedural and substantive, and the adjective owns one half.
normal.cn: 法律把世界分成程序与实体，这个形容词占一半。

normal.en: Procedure is the noun, procedural the adjective, procedurally the adverb.
normal.cn: 名词是 procedure，形容词是 procedural，副词是 procedurally。

abstract.en: Procedure is fairness made repeatable, so that the same case gets the same path.
abstract.cn: 程序是把公正做成可重复的，好让同样的案子走同样的路。

abstract.en: When procedure becomes an end in itself, the path eats the destination.
abstract.cn: 当程序本身成了目的，路径就把终点吃掉了。

abstract.en: A procedure is a promise that the next person will get the same treatment.
abstract.cn: 程序是一个承诺：下一个人也会受到同样的对待。

examples.en: The delay was procedural and did not affect the merits.
examples.cn: 这次延误属程序问题，不影响案件实体。

examples.en: Procedural fairness matters even when the answer is obvious.
examples.cn: 即使答案显而易见，程序公正仍然要紧。

examples.en: The older software was written in a procedural style.
examples.cn: 那套旧软件是过程式风格写成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普若西哲柔」——照着流程图上编号一步步走：程序的

root: procedure ＋ 形容词词尾 -al；procedure 出自拉丁语 procedere「向前走」← pro-「向前」＋ cedere「走」，同源有 proceed、process、proceeding。十六世纪进入英语，先在法律后及行政；二十世纪后期用于编程风格。形容词确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the path: the steps themselves, court rules, fairness of process, safeguards, step-by-step code, meeting order, routine behaviour, and medical procedures.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着这条路径展开：步骤本身、法庭规则、过程公正、防错保障、按步执行的代码、议事秩序、例行举止，以及医疗操作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a numbered flow chart on a wall, each box linked to the next by an arrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上贴着编号的流程图，每个方框都用箭头连到下一个。

branches.en: THE MANNER OF DOING: the steps rather than the substance, and behaviour that has become a fixed sequence.
branches.cn: 做事的方式：步骤而非实体，以及变成固定序列的举止。

branches.en: THE RULES OF THE ROOM: court rules and the motions that keep a meeting arguing about its own order.
branches.cn: 场内规则：法庭规则，以及让会议只争论自身秩序的动议。

branches.en: THE GUARDED PATH: hearing both sides, and the checks that catch a mistake before it travels.
branches.cn: 有护栏的路径：听取双方，以及错误传开之前抓住它的核查。

branches.en: THE CODE THAT READS LIKE STEPS: named sequences of instructions walked through in order.
branches.cn: 读起来像步骤的代码：按次序走过的命名指令序列。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE IN MEDICINE: what is done with hands, as distinct from diagnosis and talk.
branches.cn: 医学里的操作：动手所做之事，与诊断和谈话相区别。

intro.en: Procedural rests on the Latin verb for going forward and adds an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: procedural 依托表示「向前走」的拉丁动词，再加上英语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin procedere and the noun procedura are the sources behind the English pair procedure and procedural.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 procedere 与名词 procedura 是英语 procedure 与 procedural 这对词的来源。

items.example: The adjective marks manner rather than substance.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标的是方式而非实体。

items.example: The noun names the path as a whole.
It gives the direction of the walking.
It also stands behind process and succeed.
items.exampleCN: process 与 succeed 也由它而来。

items.example: It builds procedural, formal and substantial.
items.exampleCN: 它构成程序的、形式的与实质的等词。

items.meaning: result or manner of an act
items.exampleCN: 它构成程序与离开等词。

items.example: It builds procedurally, as in procedurally flawed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 procedurally，如程序上有瑕疵。

items.example: The plural names the whole run of steps.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式指整套步骤的进行。

latinEntries.meaning: to go forward; to come out
latinEntries.example: Latin procedere means to go forward.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 procedere 意为向前走。

latinEntries.example: Latin pro- appears in producere, to lead forward.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pro- 见于 producere（向前引出）。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb cedere (ced-, cessum; to go, yield)
latinEntries.example: Latin cedere means to go or yield, and gives cede and process.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 cedere 意为走、让步，并给出 cede 与 process。

definition_zh: v. 退化；堕落；变质 adj. 退化的；堕落的 n. 堕落者；退化者
definition_en: to become worse in quality or moral character; as an adjective, having lost good qualities; as a noun, a person who has lost moral standards
core_image: 一条原本清澈的溪流往下游走，越来越浑，最后成了泥沟
scene: 争论很快变成了辱骂。 The debate degenerated into insults.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：degenerate 指质量或品格变坏；句意是争论很快沦为辱骂。

pos.zh: 退化；堕落；变质
退化的；堕落的；变质的

definition_en: the habit or pattern of frequently being absent from work, school, or another duty
core_image: 一排工位上总有几个空位，天天如此
scene: 工厂主管翻看月度记录，发现请病假的人越来越多。 High absenteeism was slowing production at the plant.
sceneCN: 这里 absenteeism 是「旷工、缺勤现象」（第 1 个义项：员工经常不到岗的整体模式）；句意为高缺勤率正在拖慢工厂生产。

senses.title: Habitual absence from work
senses.definition: the pattern of workers regularly failing to come to work
senses.definitionCN: 员工经常不到岗的整体模式
senses.example: High absenteeism was slowing production.
senses.exampleCN: 高缺勤率正在拖慢生产。
senses.why: Absenteeism adds -ism to absentee, turning a person who is away into a collective social pattern.
senses.whyCN: absenteeism 在 absentee 后加 -ism，把「不在的人」变成一种集体的社会现象。

senses.title: Pupil absenteeism
senses.definition: the rate at which students miss school
senses.definitionCN: 学生缺课的比例或模式
senses.example: The school reported rising absenteeism in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 学校报告冬季缺课现象上升。
senses.why: The same pattern word applies to schools, where missing class is measured as a rate.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「模式」的词适用于学校，缺课在那里被当作比率衡量。

senses.title: Unexcused absence
senses.definition: absence without a valid reason, considered as a problem
senses.definitionCN: 没有正当理由的缺席，被视为问题
senses.example: The policy targets unexcused absenteeism.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策针对无正当理由的缺勤。
senses.why: The -ism suffix turns repeated unexcused absence into a recognized category for managers.
senses.whyCN: -ism 后缀把反复的无故缺席变成管理者认可的一类问题。

senses.title: Long-term absence
senses.definition: absence that continues over an extended period
senses.definitionCN: 持续较长时间的缺席
senses.example: Long-term absenteeism often follows a serious illness.
senses.exampleCN: 长期缺勤常常出现在重病之后。
senses.why: When absence lasts long enough to become a state rather than an event, the abstract noun fits.
senses.whyCN: 当缺席长到成为状态而非事件时，这个抽象名词就适用了。

senses.title: Sickness absence
senses.definition: absence attributed to illness, tracked by employers
senses.definitionCN: 归因于疾病的缺勤，由雇主统计
senses.example: Sickness absenteeism rose during the flu season.
senses.exampleCN: 流感季期间因病缺勤上升。
senses.why: Health reasons are the most common source of the pattern, so the word often appears with sickness.
senses.whyCN: 健康原因是最常见的模式来源，因此这个词常与 sickness 连用。

senses.title: An organisational problem
senses.definition: the overall level of absence treated as a management issue
senses.definitionCN: 被当作管理问题处理的整体缺席水平
senses.example: The report links absenteeism to low morale.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把缺勤与士气低落联系起来。
senses.why: Once absence is measured across a workforce, it becomes an indicator of how an organisation is doing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦在整个劳动力范围内衡量缺席，它就成为组织运行状况的指标。

senses.title: Landlord absenteeism
senses.definition: the historical pattern of owners living away from their estates
senses.definitionCN: 历史上地主不住在自己的地产上、长期不在地的现象
senses.example: The old estate suffered from landlord absenteeism.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧庄园深受不在地主现象之苦。
senses.why: The word once described owners who were absent from their land, an older sense now overshadowed by workplace use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾描述不在自己土地上的所有者，这个较早义如今被职场用法盖过。

senses.title: Absence from meetings
senses.definition: the pattern of members regularly missing meetings
senses.definitionCN: 成员经常不参加会议的模式
senses.example: Committee absenteeism delayed every vote.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会成员的缺席让每次表决都推迟。
senses.why: Any group that expects attendance can turn repeated absence into the same -ism pattern.
senses.whyCN: 任何期待出席的群体，都能把反复缺席变成同样的 -ism 现象。

intro.en: Absenteeism is a modern formation: the person noun absentee plus the suffix -ism for a practice or pattern.
intro.cn: absenteeism 是现代构词：人物名词 absentee 加表示做法或模式的后缀 -ism。

items.en: abesse meant 'to be away', from ab- 'away' and esse 'to be'.
items.cn: abesse 意为「不在、离开」，由 ab-（离开）与 esse（存在）构成。

items.en: The participle absens, 'being away', produced English absent.
items.cn: 分词 absens 意为「不在的」，构成英语 absent。

items.en: English absentee, formed with the person suffix -ee, named someone who lives away from their property or duty.
items.cn: 英语 absentee 由人物后缀 -ee 构成，指不住在自己的产业或岗位所在地的人。

items.en: The suffix -ism turns a person or practice into a named system or pattern.
items.cn: 后缀 -ism 把人物或做法变成被命名的制度或模式。

items.en: Absenteeism appeared in the nineteenth century, first often in reports about landlords who lived away from their estates.
items.cn: absenteeism 出现在十九世纪，最初常见于关于不在地主的报告。

items.en: Modern usage shifted the centre of gravity to workplaces and schools, where absenteeism is measured as a rate.
items.cn: 现代用法把重心转到职场与学校，缺勤在那里被当作比率衡量。

note.en: The first group gathers the person, adjective, and noun from which the word is built; the second gathers words for absence and skipping.
note.cn: 第一组收构成本词的人物、形容词与名词；第二组收表示缺席与逃避的词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「逃学」，指未经允许不去上学的做法。

entries.definition: The fact of not being present at an event or institution.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「未出席、未到场」。

entries.definition: The informal British word for avoiding work or duty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式非正式用语，义为「偷懒、逃避工作」。

entries.definition: A person who fails to appear when expected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爽约者、未到场者」，指应出现却没出现的人。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks build the word from absentee plus -ism and connect it to workplace metrics; the abstract hooks picture the row of empty desks.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点把词拆成 absentee 加 -ism，并联系职场指标；抽象记忆点想象一排空工位。

normal.en: Absentee plus -ism: the person who is away becomes the pattern of being away.
normal.cn: absentee 加 -ism：不在的人变成了「不在」的整体模式。

normal.en: Reduce absenteeism and absenteeism rates are standard management phrases.
normal.cn: reduce absenteeism 与 absenteeism rates 是标准管理短语。

normal.en: Sickness absenteeism separates health-related absence from other kinds.
normal.cn: sickness absenteeism 把与健康相关的缺勤与其他缺勤区分开。

normal.en: Chronic absenteeism describes a long-running pattern rather than one missed day.
normal.cn: chronic absenteeism 描述长期模式，而不是某一天没来。

normal.en: The word began with landlords who lived away from their estates.
normal.cn: 这个词最初指不住在自己庄园的地主。

abstract.en: Picture a row of desks with three chairs empty every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一排工位，每天早上都有三把椅子空着。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with the same dates crossed out month after month.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上同样的日期被一月月地划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a manager's chart with a line that refuses to fall.
abstract.cn: 想象主管的图表上有一条怎么也不下降的线。

examples.en: The company introduced new rules to reduce absenteeism.
examples.cn: 公司出台新规以减少旷工。

examples.en: Absenteeism among night-shift staff remains high.
examples.cn: 夜班员工的缺勤率仍然很高。

examples.en: Chronic absenteeism affects a child's learning.
examples.cn: 长期缺课会影响孩子的学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布森提森」——座位上的名字还在，人却一天天不来，空位成了常态。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from habitual workplace absence to schools, unexcused and long-term patterns, sickness, organisational measures, historical landlords, and meetings.

scene: 夏夜的山谷里，头顶那条乳白光带从一座山脊拖到另一座山脊，肉眼看不清其中的星点。 From the valley, the Milky Way appears as a pale band of light between the ridges.
